title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
山西鄉試錄序
今
皇上嗣登大統建元隆慶歲在丁
卯適天下大比之期先是禮
臣列議上
請以經生飾文藻鮮效用無以稱
初政求賢至意欲復體於古簡
===
士於實期以備任使於他日
制可下所司行之復用諫臣言集
廷臣議以理學名臣河東薛文
清瑄從祀孔庭蓋灼然標之
植矣士固大有幸矣哉維
時山西巡按御史王〔漸〕典監
臨事謂三晉密邇
punctuated:
山西鄉試錄序

今皇上嗣登大統，建元隆慶，歲在丁卯，適天下大比之期。先是，禮臣列議上請，以經生飾文藻、鮮效用，無以稱初政求賢至意，欲復體於古，簡士於實，期以備任使於他日。制可，下所司行之。復用諫臣言，集廷臣議，以理學名臣河東薛文清瑄從祀孔庭。蓋灼然標之植矣，士固大有幸矣哉！維時，山西巡按御史王〔漸〕典監臨事，謂三晉密邇
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shanxi Provincial Examination

His Majesty has now succeeded to the imperial throne and inaugurated the Longqing era. The year is dingmao [1567], coinciding with the triennial examinations throughout the realm. Before this, the officials of the Ministry of Rites had submitted their deliberations for imperial approval. They held that students of the Classics embellished their literary compositions but seldom demonstrated practical usefulness, and thus failed to meet the earnest desire to seek worthy men at the beginning of the reign. They wished to restore ancient standards and select men of genuine substance, so that these might be ready for appointment and service in the future. The Emperor approved and referred the matter to the responsible offices for implementation. Further, accepting the advice of a remonstrating official, he convened the court officials to deliberate on admitting Xue Xuan of Hedong, posthumously titled Wenqing, an eminent official renowned for his Learning of Principle, to accompanying worship in the temple of Confucius. Thus a standard was conspicuously established [?]. How fortunate indeed were the scholars!

At this time, Wang Jian 王〔漸〕, Regional Inspector of Shanxi, was serving as Supervising Official. He observed that the Three Jin [Shanxi] lay very close to…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
畿輔宜祇承
德意爲諸藩先秉虔虔禮聘儒
碩以〔學末〕與〔進〕典教諭王典考
試事教授紀〔文煒〕張〔承芳〕程
〔允中〕徐〔騰〕典同考試事布政
司左布政使李〔僑〕右叅政劉
〔日林〕典提調事按察司副使
===
郭〔斗〕僉事沈〔人种〕典監試事
選其屬之賢者典諸司事旣
入院矢公矢明內外之務罔
不慎毖合提學副使陳〔端〕暨
大同僉事武〔建邦〕所簡士一
千九百有奇三試之遵
制取六十五人幷其文之近古而
punctuated: 畿輔，宜祇承德意，爲諸藩先。秉虔虔，禮聘儒碩，以〔學末〕與〔進〕典教諭王典考試事，教授紀〔文煒〕、張〔承芳〕、程〔允中〕、徐〔騰〕典同考試事，布政司左布政使李〔僑〕、右叅政劉〔日林〕典提調事，按察司副使郭〔斗〕、僉事沈〔人种〕典監試事。選其屬之賢者典諸司事。旣入院，矢公矢明，內外之務罔不慎毖。合提學副使陳〔端〕暨大同僉事武〔建邦〕所簡士一千九百有奇，三試之，遵制取六十五人，幷其文之近古而
translation_en:
…the metropolitan region, and should therefore reverently uphold the imperial intentions and take the lead among the provinces. With deep reverence, he formally invited eminent scholars, entrusting the duties of Examiner to this humble scholar [?] and Instructor Wang [the sequence 〔進〕典教諭王 is doubtful]. Prefectural School Instructors Ji Wenwei, Zhang Chengfang, Cheng Yunzhong, and Xu Teng served as Associate Examiners. Li Qiao, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Liu Rilin, Right Administration Adviser, served as Proctors. Guo Dou, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, and Shen Renzhong, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, supervised the examination. Worthy men were selected from among their subordinates to oversee the various offices. Upon entering the examination compound, they pledged impartiality and discernment; every matter, within and outside the compound, received meticulous attention.
The candidates selected by Chen Duan, Surveillance Vice Commissioner and Education Intendant, together with Wu Jianbang, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner at Datong, numbered more than nineteen hundred in all. They were examined in three sessions, and sixty-five were selected in accordance with the imperial regulations, together with those of their compositions that followed ancient models and …

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
理優者錄成以
獻〔學 朱〕濫竽文柄於多士有一
日之雅乃進而告之曰子多
士既舉於鄉矣行且敷對
大廷爲
天子使抑知
上之所以求與所以自待之義乎
===
皇上睿智夙成
孝慈純備
臨馭以來振舉宏綱恢弘化理
覃鴻恩於宇內
敷文德於殊俗其於事
天之敬逮下之仁蓋兢兢焉無時
或豫矣
punctuated:
理優者，錄成以獻。〔學 朱〕濫竽文柄，於多士有一日之雅，乃進而告之曰：「子多士既舉於鄉矣，行且敷對大廷，爲天子使。抑知上之所以求與所以自待之義乎？

皇上睿智夙成，孝慈純備。臨馭以來，振舉宏綱，恢弘化理，覃鴻恩於宇內，敷文德於殊俗。其於事天之敬、逮下之仁，蓋兢兢焉，無時或豫矣。
translation_en:
…those superior in reasoning were compiled into a record for presentation to the throne. We, Xue and Zhu [?], unworthily entrusted with authority over literary assessment, have had a brief acquaintance with you scholars. We therefore came forward and addressed you: “You scholars have now been selected in the Provincial Examination. Soon you will present your answers before the imperial court and serve as the Son of Heaven’s emissaries. But do you understand what His Majesty seeks in you and what you ought to expect of yourselves?

“His Majesty’s penetrating wisdom matured early, and his filial devotion and benevolence are complete and pure. Since ascending the throne, he has invigorated the great principles of government and extended the transforming influence of his rule, spreading abundant grace throughout the realm and civil virtue among peoples of different customs. In his reverence in serving Heaven and his benevolence toward those below, he has remained ever vigilant, never allowing himself a moment of ease.

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
萬幾有暇卽
御講幄親儒臣究六藝之精藴考
聖哲之懿軌而又表亮節之
士隆理學之臣毅然必以堯
舜爲法思得所以佐唐虞之
治者而用之於兹首舉特愼
重焉于多士乃際斯會可不
謂榮幸大與易謂雲從龍風
從虎聖人作而萬物覩多士
===
仰
堯舜之在上自待其身舍唐虞之
佐奚以哉夫晉放勳重華之
故都也内而恒霍鎭立太行
拱峙汾絳環匯外而華嶽聳
punctuated:
萬幾有暇，卽御講幄，親儒臣，究六藝之精藴，考聖哲之懿軌，而又表亮節之士，隆理學之臣，毅然必以堯舜爲法，思得所以佐唐虞之治者而用之。於兹首舉，特愼重焉。于多士乃際斯會，可不謂榮幸大與？《易》謂：「雲從龍，風從虎，聖人作而萬物覩。」多士仰堯舜之在上，自待其身，舍唐虞之佐奚以哉？

夫晉，放勳重華之故都也。内而恒霍鎭立，太行拱峙，汾絳環匯；外而華嶽聳
translation_en:
Whenever he has leisure amid the myriad affairs of state, His Majesty proceeds to the lecture chamber, draws Confucian officials close, investigates the profound essence of the Six Arts, and examines the admirable precedents of the sages and worthies. He also honors men of lofty integrity and esteems officials devoted to the Learning of Principle. Firmly resolved to take Yao and Shun as his models, he seeks men capable of assisting a government like that of Tang and Yu and employs them. He has exercised particular care over this first examination of his reign. You assembled scholars [?], encountering such an occasion, may surely call your honor and good fortune great! The Book of Changes says: “Clouds follow the dragon; winds follow the tiger. The sage arises, and all creatures behold him.” As you scholars look up to a Yao or Shun upon the throne, what standard should you set for yourselves other than that of the ministers who assisted Tang and Yu?

Now Jin was the seat of the ancient capitals of Fangxun and Chonghua—that is, Yao and Shun. Within it, Mount Heng and Mount Huo stand as guardians, the Taihang Mountains rise as if in respectful attendance, and the Fen and Jiang rivers encircle and converge; beyond it, Mount Hua towers…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
其右泰山昴其左少室參其
前大河縈其襟宋儒謂爲天
下奥區眞達觀之矣其在唐
虞則有臯夔稷契都喩吁咈
以佐聖治功成配天利賴永
世不可尚已下至春秋如狐
趙輩左右其君猶能取威定
霸主中國會盟雖其功烈所
===
就視帝臣王佐未敢儷焉然
亦瓌瑋奇傑之士矣豈非河
嶽英靈扶輿清淑之氣發紓
於人文者哉我
朝奠鼎燕京晉爲近服
祖宗德澤之培
punctuated:
其右，泰山昴其左，少室參其前，大河縈其襟。宋儒謂爲天下奥區，眞達觀之矣。其在唐虞，則有臯、夔、稷、契，都喩吁咈，以佐聖治，功成配天，利賴永世，不可尚已。下至春秋，如狐、趙輩，左右其君，猶能取威定霸，主中國會盟。雖其功烈所就，視帝臣王佐，未敢儷焉，然亦瓌瑋奇傑之士矣。豈非河嶽英靈、扶輿清淑之氣，發紓於人文者哉？
我朝奠鼎燕京，晉爲近服。祖宗德澤之培
translation_en:
…to its right, with Mount Tai rising [?] to its left, Mount Shaoshi standing before it, and the Great River winding about its lap. The Confucian scholars of the Song called it a secluded heartland of the realm: theirs was truly a penetrating judgment. In the days of Tang and Yu, there were Gao, Kui, Ji, and Xie, whose words of approval, instruction, caution, and remonstrance [?] assisted the sages’ governance. Their achievements matched Heaven, and their benefits sustained all subsequent ages; nothing could surpass them. Even later, in the Spring and Autumn period, men such as Hu and Zhao assisted their rulers and could still establish their authority and secure their hegemony, presiding over covenant assemblies of the central states. Although their accomplishments could not presume to equal those of the ministers of the sage emperors and the helpers of the sage kings, they too were men of extraordinary distinction. Was this not the spiritual potency of the rivers and mountains, their accumulated pure and harmonious vital force, finding expression in human culture?
Our dynasty established its capital at Yanjing, and Jin became a territory close to the capital. The nurturing bestowed by the virtue and beneficence of our imperial ancestors…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
列聖敎化之洽旣愽且厚一時豪
傑之士勃然而興未易更僕
至文清薛氏崛起河東究析
精微踐履純篤爲
國朝理學第一咸以承源朱許
上接孔孟之傳要非過論玆
又所謂卓然絶類冠倫者也
===
其所著述載之讀書從政二
錄總若干萬言大旨則在持
敬求仁以堯舜君民爲極致
子多士其鄉之後學也景行
先哲誦法章程亦旣有年矣
肆觀所爲文析理義則奥而
精論治道則弘而要考事功
punctuated:
列聖敎化之洽，旣愽且厚，一時豪傑之士勃然而興，未易更僕。至文清薛氏崛起河東，究析精微，踐履純篤，爲國朝理學第一，咸以承源朱許，上接孔孟之傳，要非過論。玆又所謂卓然絶類冠倫者也。
其所著述，載之《讀書》《從政》二錄，總若干萬言，大旨則在持敬求仁，以堯舜君民爲極致。子多士，其鄉之後學也，景行先哲，誦法章程，亦旣有年矣。肆觀所爲文，析理義則奥而精，論治道則弘而要，考事功
translation_en:
…the pervasive moral instruction of successive sage emperors has been both broad and profound. Outstanding men arose vigorously in that age, too numerous to enumerate readily, even with successive attendants taking turns. Then Master Xue, honored as Wenqing, emerged in Hedong. He investigated and analyzed the most subtle principles, and his practice was pure and steadfast, making him foremost in the Learning of Principle in our dynasty. All regarded him as drawing upon Zhu and Xu and, through them, continuing the transmission from Confucius and Mencius. This judgment was certainly no exaggeration. Here indeed was one who stood conspicuously above his kind and surpassed his peers.
His writings are contained in the two records, the Record of Reading and the Record of Government Service, totaling some tens of thousands of words. Their central purpose lies in maintaining reverence and seeking humaneness, with making the ruler and people like those of Yao and Shun as the highest attainment. You scholars [?] are later students from his native region. For years now, you have admired and followed this earlier worthy, reciting his teachings and taking his precepts as your model. Examining your compositions, I find that your analyses of moral principles are profound and precise, and your discussions of the Way of governance broad and focused on essentials; in assessing practical achievements…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
則正而確秩乎其章郁乎其
采所得於文清者居多主司
輒嘆服不置曰茲三晉之英
也豫養之所得也他日輔
堯舜之君以成唐虞之治或在於
此未嘗不津津然喜然貌質
殊情華實異致自古患之則
復惴惴然懼即多士自待誠
===
厚以無負於
初政之求無乖於鄉先哲之誼
則於所謂敬與仁加之意耳
夫敬德之聚仁善之長薛氏
論之詳矣自一念之微以至
於百爲之著俾此心無少間
punctuated:
則正而確，秩乎其章，郁乎其采，所得於文清者居多。主司輒嘆服不置，曰：「茲三晉之英也，豫養之所得也。他日輔堯舜之君，以成唐虞之治，或在於此。」未嘗不津津然喜。然貌質殊情，華實異致，自古患之，則復惴惴然懼。即多士自待誠厚，以無負於初政之求，無乖於鄉先哲之誼，則於所謂敬與仁加之意耳。
夫敬，德之聚；仁，善之長。薛氏論之詳矣。自一念之微，以至於百爲之著，俾此心無少間
translation_en:
…are sound and precise. Their compositions are orderly in structure and rich in literary expression; much of what they have learned derives from Wenqing. The presiding examiners repeatedly expressed unceasing admiration, saying: “These are the outstanding talents of Sanjin [Shanxi], the fruits of prior cultivation. Those who will one day assist a ruler like Yao or Shun in achieving the good government of Tang and Yu may well be among them.” I could not but feel delighted. Yet outward appearance and inner substance may differ, and literary flowering and actual fruit may diverge—an enduring concern since antiquity. Thus I also felt apprehensive. If you scholars truly set high expectations for yourselves, seeking neither to disappoint the aspirations of this new reign nor to depart from the principles of your region’s earlier worthy, you need only devote greater attention to what are called reverent attentiveness and humaneness.
Reverent attentiveness is where virtue gathers; humaneness is foremost among good qualities. Master Xue has discussed these in detail. From the subtlety of a single thought to the manifest expression of a hundred actions, let this mind suffer not the slightest interruption…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
斷斯可以言敬自一物之小
以至於九有之大俾此心無
少睽隔斯可以言仁敬以立
體而未甞不達之用仁以及
物而未甞不本之身茲固合
內外而宜時措之道也予多
士隱居求志熟識所謂敬與
===
仁已繼自今出而用世非敬
罔存非仁罔行卑霸習而崇
聖道以底於極致使是
君為堯舜之君是民為堯舜之民
是身為臯夔稷契之身斯為
有光於其鄉克對
聖天子崇重理學之休命而主司
punctuated: 斷，斯可以言敬；自一物之小，以至於九有之大，俾此心無少睽隔，斯可以言仁。敬以立體，而未甞不達之用；仁以及物，而未甞不本之身。茲固合內外而宜時措之道也。予多士隱居求志，熟識所謂敬與仁已。繼自今出而用世，非敬罔存，非仁罔行，卑霸習而崇聖道，以底於極致，使是君為堯舜之君，是民為堯舜之民，是身為臯夔稷契之身，斯為有光於其鄉，克對聖天子崇重理學之休命，而主司
translation_en:
…interruption: only then can one speak of reverent attentiveness. From the smallest single thing to the vastness of the Nine Regions, let this mind remain free of the slightest estrangement: only then can one speak of benevolence. Reverent attentiveness establishes the essential foundation, yet invariably extends into practical functioning; benevolence reaches out to things, yet invariably takes its root in oneself. This, indeed, is the Way that unites inner and outer and is fittingly put into practice as circumstances require.

You, my scholars, have lived in retirement to pursue your aspirations and are already thoroughly acquainted with what is meant by reverent attentiveness and benevolence. Henceforth, when you emerge to serve the world, preserve nothing that is without reverent attentiveness and undertake nothing that is without benevolence. Esteem lightly the practices of hegemony and exalt the Way of the sages, thereby attaining the highest perfection. Make this ruler a ruler like Yao and Shun, these people a people like those of Yao and Shun, and yourselves men like Gao, Kui, Ji, and Xie. In this way you will bring honor to your native province and worthily answer the sage Son of Heaven’s gracious command to honor the Learning of Principle, while the examination administrators…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
奉
德意以翊
初政可塞於萬一矣予多士勗
哉御史與〔學朱〕等日切望之
是舉也克振壯猷惕懆多士
時則有若總督軍務兵部左
侍郎兼都察院右僉都御史
===
王〔之誥〕巡撫山西右僉都御
史王〔繼洛〕巡撫大同右僉都
御史張〔志孝〕懋揚風紀作興
多士時則有若巡按宣大御
史周〔詠〕巡鹽御史趙〔睿〕肅將
王命適觀多士時則有若刑科
都給事中朱〔繪〕兵科給事中
punctuated:
奉德意以翊初政，可塞於萬一矣。予多士勗哉！御史與〔學朱〕等日切望之。
是舉也，克振壯猷，惕懆多士，時則有若總督軍務兵部左侍郎兼都察院右僉都御史王〔之誥〕、巡撫山西右僉都御史王〔繼洛〕、巡撫大同右僉都御史張〔志孝〕；懋揚風紀，作興多士，時則有若巡按宣大御史周〔詠〕、巡鹽御史趙〔睿〕；肅將王命，適觀多士，時則有若刑科都給事中朱〔繪〕、兵科給事中
translation_en:
…in carrying out the emperor’s gracious intentions and assisting his newly inaugurated government, might discharge one ten-thousandth of their obligation. You scholars, exert yourselves! The censor, together with Xuezhu [?] and the others, earnestly hopes for this every day.
For this examination, those who vigorously advanced great plans and stirred the assembled scholars to watchful diligence included Wang Zhigao, Supreme Commander of Military Affairs, Left Vice Minister of War, and concurrently Right Assistant Censor-in-chief of the Censorate; Wang Jiluo, Grand Coordinator of Shanxi and Right Assistant Censor-in-chief; and Zhang Zhixiao, Grand Coordinator of Datong and Right Assistant Censor-in-chief. Those who assiduously upheld discipline and inspired the assembled scholars included Zhou Yong, Regional Inspecting Censor for Xuanfu and Datong, and Zhao Rui, Salt-inspecting Censor. Those who reverently carried out the imperial commands and happened to observe the assembled scholars included Zhu Hui, Chief Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Justice, and the Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for War …

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
張〔齊〕巡按直隸監察御史趙
〔岩〕刑部郎中陳〔忠翰〕相與贊
襄嘉樂多士時則有若總理
糧儲戶部郎中張〔來可〕主事
王〔汝梅〕右布政使楊〔振高〕左
參政宋〔岳〕右參政趙〔格〕羅〔瑤〕
右參議周〔斯盛〕秦〔可大〕副使
===
王〔學謨〕孫〔一正〕廖〔逢節〕楊〔旂〕
范〔大儒〕黃〔正色〕楊〔銖〕曹〔金〕僉

translation_en:
… Zhang Qi; Zhao Yan, Investigating Censor inspecting Zhili; and Chen Zhonghan, Director in the Ministry of Justice.

Among those who jointly lent their assistance and encouraged and delighted in the assembled scholars were the following. Zhang Laike was Director in the Ministry of Revenue, with overall responsibility for grain reserves; Wang Rumei was a Secretary. Yang Zhengao was Right Provincial Administration Commissioner. Song Yue was Left Administration Vice Commissioner; Zhao Ge and Luo Yao were Right Administration Vice Commissioners. Zhou Sisheng and Qin Keda were Right Assistant Administration Commissioners. Wang Xuemo, Sun Yizheng, Liao Fengjie, Yang Qi, Fan Daru, Huang Zhengse, Yang Zhu, and Cao Jin were Surveillance Vice Commissioners. Ge Daji, Qiu Wenxue, and Li Chun were Assistant Surveillance Commissioners. Shen Weiyue was Regional Commander; Ji Dong was Assistant Regional Commander. Huang Long, Shao Liang, and Liu Fengxiang were acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners.

At that time, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Li Fengshi had just arrived. In accordance with the prescribed practice, all could be recorded here.

印卷官
translation_en:
Shanxi Provincial Examination, First Year of Longqing (1567)

Supervising Official
Wang Jian, Investigating Censor assigned to inspect Shanxi, had the courtesy name Sijin and was from Wei County, Shandong. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the guichou year.

Proctors
Li Qiao, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shanxi, had the courtesy name Zigao and was from Changqing County, Shandong. He became a metropolitan graduate in the jiachen year.
Liu Ricai, Right Administration Vice Commissioner of Shanxi, had the courtesy name Rucheng and was from Nanchang County, Jiangxi. He became a metropolitan graduate in the guichou year.

Examination Monitoring Officials
Guo Dou, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Shanxi, had the courtesy name Yingxiu. He was registered in an officer household of the Yunnan Right Guard and was a native of Fengqiu County, Henan. He became a metropolitan graduate in the guichou year.
Shen Renzhong, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Shanxi, had the courtesy name Shiyong and was from Jiading County, Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate in the jiwei year.

Examiners
Liu Xuezhu, Instructor at the Confucian School of Taoyuan County, Huai’an Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Daoming and was from Luling County, Jiangxi. He became a tribute scholar (gongshi) in the wuwu year.
Wang Jin, Instructor at the Confucian School of Chengwu County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, had the courtesy name Deqing and was from Anfu County, Jiangxi. He became a tribute scholar in the yimao year.

Associate Examiners
Ji Wenwei, Professor at the Confucian School of Daming Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Cunyang and was from Yulin Guard, Shaanxi. He became a tribute scholar in the guimao year.
Zhang Chengfang, Professor at the Confucian School of Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, had the courtesy name Rujing and was from Chao County, Zhili. He became a tribute scholar in the gengzi year.
Cheng Yunzhong, Professor at the Confucian School of Nanyang Prefecture, Henan, had the courtesy name Yidao and was from Jiyang County, Shandong. He became a tribute scholar in the gengzi year.
Xu Teng, Professor at the Confucian School of Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Zida and was registered in an artisan household of the Construction Office. He was a native of Chongde County, Zhejiang, and became a tribute scholar in the bingwu year.

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰爲政以德譬如北辰居其所而衆星
共之
敬大臣也體羣臣也
及其聞一善言見一善行若決江河沛然
莫之能禦也
易
乾元者始而亨者也
===
六五鼎黄耳金鉉利貞象曰鼎黄耳中以
爲實也上九鼎玉鉉大吉无不利象曰
玉鉉在上剛柔節也
易其至矣乎夫易聖人所以崇德而廣業
也知崇禮卑崇效天卑法地
齊也者言萬物之潔齊也
書
在知人在安民
明王奉若天道
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子曰：「爲政以德，譬如北辰，居其所而衆星共之。」

敬大臣也，體羣臣也。

及其聞一善言，見一善行，若決江河，沛然莫之能禦也。

易

乾元者，始而亨者也。

六五，鼎黄耳金鉉，利貞。象曰：「鼎黄耳，中以爲實也。」上九，鼎玉鉉，大吉，无不利。象曰：「玉鉉在上，剛柔節也。」

易其至矣乎！夫易，聖人所以崇德而廣業也。知崇禮卑，崇效天，卑法地。

齊也者，言萬物之潔齊也。

書

在知人，在安民。

明王奉若天道。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said: “Governing through virtue is like the Pole Star: it remains in its place while all the other stars turn toward it.”

Respect the great ministers and show sympathetic consideration for the body of officials.

When he heard a single good saying or witnessed a single good deed, he was like the Yangzi and Yellow Rivers bursting their banks, surging onward with a force that none could withstand.

Book of Changes

The primal power of Qian is that which initiates and brings things to flourishing.

Six in the fifth place: The cauldron has yellow handles and a metal carrying bar. Constancy is beneficial. The Image says: “The cauldron’s yellow handles signify that centrality constitutes its substance.” Nine at the top: The cauldron has a jade carrying bar. Great good fortune; nothing is unfavorable. The Image says: “The jade carrying bar is at the top: firmness and yielding are properly regulated.”

How consummate are the Changes! The Changes are the means by which the sages exalt their virtue and enlarge their achievements. Knowledge is lofty; ritual propriety is humble. Loftiness follows the example of Heaven; humility takes Earth as its model.

‘Putting in order’ means that the myriad things are purified and brought into order.

Book of Documents

It lies in knowing people and in bringing peace to the people.

The enlightened king reverently follows the Way of Heaven.

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
初一曰五行次二曰敬用五事
立政任人準夫牧作三事虎賁綴衣趣馬
小尹左右攜僕百司庶府大都小伯藝
人表臣百司太史尹伯庶常吉士司徒
司馬司空亞旅夷微盧烝三亳阪尹
詩
我稼既同上入執宮功晝爾于茅宵爾索
綯亟其乘屋其始播百穀
彼爾維何維常之華彼路斯何君子之車
戎車既駕四牡業業豈敢定居一月三
===
捷
永言孝思昭哉嗣服
殷受命咸宜百祿是何
春秋
春天王使南季來聘〔隱公九年〕單伯至自
齊〔文公十有五年〕
八月公會齊侯宋公鄭伯曹伯邾人于檉
〔僖公元年〕
punctuated:
初一曰五行，次二曰敬用五事。

立政：任人、準夫、牧，作三事。虎賁、綴衣、趣馬、小尹、左右攜僕、百司、庶府、大都、小伯、藝人、表臣、百司、太史、尹伯、庶常吉士、司徒、司馬、司空、亞旅、夷、微、盧烝、三亳阪尹。

詩

我稼既同，上入執宮功。晝爾于茅，宵爾索綯。亟其乘屋，其始播百穀。

彼爾維何？維常之華。彼路斯何？君子之車。戎車既駕，四牡業業。豈敢定居？一月三捷。

永言孝思，昭哉嗣服。

殷受命咸宜，百祿是何。

春秋

春，天王使南季來聘。〔隱公九年〕單伯至自齊。〔文公十有五年〕

八月，公會齊侯、宋公、鄭伯、曹伯、邾人于檉。〔僖公元年〕
translation_en:
First are the Five Elements; second is the reverent employment of the Five Activities.

In establishing government, those entrusted with appointments, those responsible for judicial standards, and the regional governors constitute the three chief offices. There are the Tiger Guards, keepers of the royal robes, supervisors of horses, minor administrators, attendant servants on the left and right, the various officials, the many storehouse officers, officials of the great cities, lesser chiefs, artisans, ministers outside the court, the various officials, the Grand Scribe, administrative chiefs, the many regular officers of proven worth, the Minister of Education, the Minister of War, the Minister of Works, subordinate officers, the peoples of Yi, Wei, and Lu, and the administrators of the Three Bo and the hills [?].

Book of Odes

Our crops have all been gathered; we go up into the settlement to work on the buildings. By day gather thatching grass; by night twist ropes. Hurry up onto the roofs to repair them, for soon you must begin sowing the various grains.

What is that luxuriant blossom? It is the flower of the cherry tree. What is that great carriage? It is the commander's chariot. The war chariot is already harnessed; its four stallions are mighty. How dare we remain at rest? In one month, three victories.

Ever cherish thoughts of filial devotion: how illustriously you carry on your inherited duties!

Yin received the Mandate, fittingly in every respect; it bears the hundred blessings.

Spring and Autumn Annals

In spring, the Heavenly King sent Nan Ji on a diplomatic visit to our state. 〔Ninth year of Duke Yin.〕 The Earl of Shan returned from Qi. 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Wen.〕

In the eighth month, the duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, and a representative of Zhu at Cheng. 〔First year of Duke Xi.〕

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
春王正月公會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯
許男曹伯侵蔡蔡潰遂伐楚次于陘〔僖〕
〔公四年〕晉欒書帥師救鄭〔成公六年〕公
會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊世子光莒子
邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭會于
蕭魚〔襄公十有一年〕
宋公陳侯衛侯曹伯會晉師于棐林伐鄭
〔宣公元年〕公會晉師于瓦〔定公八年〕
禮記
樂由陽來者也禮由陰作者也陰陽和而
===
萬物得
紀綱既正天下大定
唯聖人爲能饗帝孝子爲能饗親
氣如白虹天也精神見于山川地也
第貳場
論
君道以至誠仁愛爲本
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
punctuated:
春，王正月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡，蔡潰，遂伐楚，次于陘〔僖〕〔公四年〕。晉欒書帥師救鄭〔成公六年〕。公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，會于蕭魚〔襄公十有一年〕。
宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯會晉師于棐林伐鄭〔宣公元年〕。公會晉師于瓦〔定公八年〕。
禮記
樂由陽來者也，禮由陰作者也。陰陽和而萬物得。
紀綱既正，天下大定。
唯聖人爲能饗帝，孝子爲能饗親。
氣如白虹，天也；精神見于山川，地也。
第貳場
論
君道以至誠仁愛爲本。
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
translation_en:
In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the duke joined the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao in invading Cai. Cai collapsed. They then attacked Chu and encamped at Xing. [Fourth year of Duke Xi.] Luan Shu of Jin led an army to relieve Zheng. [Sixth year of Duke Cheng.] The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Xiaozhu in attacking Zheng. They assembled at Xiaoyu. [Eleventh year of Duke Xiang.]
The Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao joined the army of Jin at Feilin to attack Zheng. [First year of Duke Xuan.] The duke joined the army of Jin at Wa. [Eighth year of Duke Ding.]
Record of Rites (Liji)
Music comes from yang; ritual arises from yin. When yin and yang are harmonious, all things attain their proper condition.
Once the governing principles are set right, all under Heaven is firmly settled.
Only a sage can offer sacrifice to the Lord on High; only a filial son can offer sacrifice to his parents.
The vital force is like a white rainbow: this pertains to Heaven. Spiritual essence manifests itself in mountains and rivers: this pertains to Earth.
Second Session
Discourse
The way of the ruler takes utmost sincerity, benevolence, and love as its foundation.
Edicts, proclamations, and memorials [One question from among these [?].]

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
擬漢令司隸刺史歲考長吏殿最以聞詔〔永平九年〕
擬唐加左僕射房玄齡太子少師誥〔貞觀十三年〕
擬
皇上初
御經筵羣臣
賀表
判語五條
===
稱乘輿車駕
官文書稽程
市司評物價
宿衛人兵仗
斷罪引律令
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問帝王致治之盛未有不本於學者粤稽
唐虞執中成周建極聖學傳心之要具
punctuated:
擬漢令司隸刺史歲考長吏殿最以聞詔〔永平九年〕。
擬唐加左僕射房玄齡太子少師誥〔貞觀十三年〕。
擬皇上初御經筵羣臣賀表。
判語五條：
稱乘輿車駕；官文書稽程；市司評物價；宿衛人兵仗；斷罪引律令。
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問：帝王致治之盛，未有不本於學者。粤稽唐虞執中，成周建極，聖學傳心之要具
translation_en:
Draft an edict of the Han dynasty ordering the Metropolitan Inspector to assess annually the best and worst performance of senior local officials and report to the throne. 〔Ninth year of Yongping〕
Draft a proclamation of the Tang dynasty conferring on Fang Xuanling, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, the additional title of Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent. 〔Thirteenth year of Zhenguan〕
Draft a congratulatory memorial from the assembled officials on His Majesty’s first attendance at the Classics Colloquium.
Five legal judgments:
Use of the terms “Imperial Conveyance” and “Imperial Carriage”; delays beyond prescribed time limits in processing official documents; assessment of commodity prices by market officials; weapons of palace guards; citation of statutes and ordinances in determining sentences.
Third Session
Policy Questions 〔Five questions〕
Question: No emperor or king has ever brought government to its highest flourishing without grounding it in learning. Looking back to antiquity, Yao and Shun held fast to the Mean, and the Zhou established the supreme standard. The essentials of the learning of the sages, transmitted from mind to mind, are fully …

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
在後世若虎觀石渠集賢崇正漢唐宋
諸君志亦勤矣而治不古若何與豈古
帝王之學未之有得與洪惟我
太祖高皇帝肇造區夏日親儒臣若
論家人洪範
論大學論孟妙契千古聖人之蘊及恭覩
觀心有亭
存心有錄
聖政首篇有述則
===
太祖之學眞古帝王正心之學也暨我
皇考世宗肅皇帝丕承鴻業詢謀輔臣若揭
九五
恭默書
豳風
無逸銳意千古聖人之訓及莊誦
敬一有箴
心箴有註經書備覽有詩則
皇考之學郎
punctuated: 在。後世若虎觀、石渠、集賢、崇正，漢、唐、宋諸君志亦勤矣，而治不古若，何與？豈古帝王之學未之有得與？洪惟我太祖高皇帝肇造區夏，日親儒臣，若論《家人》《洪範》，論《大學》《論》《孟》，妙契千古聖人之蘊。及恭覩觀心有亭，存心有錄，《聖政》首篇有述，則太祖之學眞古帝王正心之學也。暨我皇考世宗肅皇帝丕承鴻業，詢謀輔臣，若揭「九五」「恭默」，書《豳風》《無逸》，銳意千古聖人之訓。及莊誦《敬一》有箴，《心箴》有註，《經書備覽》有詩，則皇考之學郎
translation_en:
… are fully present. In later ages there were such institutions as the Tiger Pavilion, the Stone Canal Pavilion, the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, and the Chongzheng Hall. The rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song were likewise diligent in their aspirations; why, then, did their government fall short of antiquity? Was it because they had not grasped the learning of the ancient sage kings?
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao, when founding his realm in the Chinese lands, daily associated with Confucian ministers. In discussing the Family hexagram, the Great Plan, the Great Learning, the Analects, and the Mencius, he wondrously apprehended the profound meaning of the sages through the ages. Moreover, we respectfully observe that there was a pavilion for contemplating the mind, a record on preserving the mind, and an account in the opening chapter of Sagely Government. Thus Taizu’s learning was truly the learning of the ancient sage kings in rectifying the mind.
Then our imperial father, Emperor Shizong Su, magnificently inherited this great undertaking and consulted his assisting ministers. He displayed the words “Nine in the fifth place” and “Reverent silence” [?], and wrote out the Airs of Bin and Against Idleness, earnestly applying himself to the teachings of the sages through the ages. Moreover, we solemnly recite his Admonition on Reverencing the One, his annotations to the Admonition on the Mind, and his poems in the Comprehensive Survey of the Classics. Thus the learning of our imperial father [is?] …

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
太祖正心之學也
聖祖
神孫授受一道用成隆古之治不可尚矣恭惟
我
皇上嗣承大統首開
經筵
躬幸胄監仰窺緝熙
聖學之心紹
祖考而追唐虞衍千萬世道統之傳丕隆治化
===
端在
今日矣顧人臣啓沃之忠不自已也諸士子
行懷靖獻當必有能敷陳帝道對揚
先訓者願敬述之爲
聖天子典學之助
問人道大端曰忠與孝昔人論忠孝之大
者必歸諸舜與周公固所以立子道臣
道之極卓乎不可尚已嘗考諸論記所
載有分忠孝爲二者有合忠孝爲一者
punctuated:
太祖正心之學也。聖祖神孫，授受一道，用成隆古之治，不可尚矣。恭惟我皇上嗣承大統，首開經筵，躬幸胄監，仰窺緝熙聖學之心，紹祖考而追唐虞，衍千萬世道統之傳，丕隆治化，端在今日矣。顧人臣啓沃之忠，不自已也。諸士子行懷靖獻，當必有能敷陳帝道、對揚先訓者，願敬述之，爲聖天子典學之助。
問：人道大端，曰忠與孝。昔人論忠孝之大者，必歸諸舜與周公，固所以立子道、臣道之極，卓乎不可尚已。嘗考諸《論》《記》所載，有分忠孝爲二者，有合忠孝爲一者。
translation_en:
…the learning of Taizu in rectifying the mind. The sagely ancestor and his divine descendant transmitted and received the same Way, thereby achieving a government comparable to that of high antiquity, unsurpassable indeed. We reverently reflect that our emperor, upon succeeding to the imperial rule, first convened the Classics Colloquium and personally visited the Directorate of Education. We look up and discern his resolve continually to illuminate his sagely learning. To carry on the work of his ancestors and his late father, emulate Tang Yao and Yu Shun, extend the transmission of the succession of the Way through countless generations, and greatly advance good government and moral transformation—these depend precisely upon the present day. Yet a minister’s loyal desire to enlighten and nourish his sovereign’s mind cannot be restrained. You examination candidates aspire to offer your devoted service; surely among you are those able to expound the Way of the true king and worthily proclaim the teachings handed down. Please set these forth reverently, to assist the sagely Son of Heaven in his constant pursuit of learning.
Question: The great essentials of the human Way are loyalty and filial piety. When men of former times discussed the highest expressions of loyalty and filial piety, they invariably attributed them to Shun and the Duke of Zhou. In doing so, they established the supreme standards for the duties of son and minister, towering beyond all possibility of surpassing them. I have examined what is recorded in the Analects and the Record of Rites: some passages distinguish loyalty and filial piety as two things, while others unite them as one…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
何其言之不同與或者分雖殊而理則
一固相通而不悖與孝經一書成於曾
子門人之手言自天子至於庶人皆以
孝爲先後世乃有擬作忠經者而觀其
論列又不專爲人臣者訓果與孝經相
爲表裏否與抑别有所可議者與我
國家誕敷懿教治本綱常
列聖相承嘗纂輯
孝順事實
===
歷代臣鑒二書以勸戒天下之爲人臣子者
至矣其宏綱要旨有互相發明者可鋪
張而揄揚之與諸士子行且服官移孝
爲忠者也況躬逢
今上御極之初正臣子奮勵之日願以素所講
明者著於篇將覘爾他日之效用何如
也
問人才之盛嘗因乎治道惟兹全晉當唐
虞三代盛時彬彬多才士秉德樹勛邈
punctuated:
何其言之不同與？或者分雖殊，而理則一，固相通而不悖與？《孝經》一書成於曾子門人之手，言自天子至於庶人皆以孝爲先。後世乃有擬作《忠經》者，而觀其論列，又不專爲人臣者訓，果與《孝經》相爲表裏否與？抑别有所可議者與？我國家誕敷懿教，治本綱常。列聖相承，嘗纂輯《孝順事實》《歷代臣鑒》二書，以勸戒天下之爲人臣子者，至矣。其宏綱要旨有互相發明者，可鋪張而揄揚之與？諸士子行且服官，移孝爲忠者也。況躬逢今上御極之初，正臣子奮勵之日，願以素所講明者著於篇，將覘爾他日之效用何如也。
問：人才之盛嘗因乎治道。惟兹全晉，當唐虞三代盛時，彬彬多才士，秉德樹勛，邈
translation_en:
…Why do these statements differ? Might it be that, although the respective duties differ, their underlying principle is one, so that they are indeed interconnected and do not conflict? The Classic of Filial Piety (Xiaojing), compiled by the disciples of Zengzi, states that everyone, from the Son of Heaven down to the common people, takes filial piety as foremost. In later ages, some composed a Classic of Loyalty (Zhongjing) in imitation of it. Yet, examining its arguments, we find that its instructions are not directed exclusively to ministers. Does it truly complement the Classic of Filial Piety, as the outer and inner aspects of a single whole? Or are there other points open to question? Our dynasty has broadly disseminated its excellent teachings, grounding government in the cardinal relationships and constant virtues. Successive sage emperors have compiled the two books, Factual Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi) and Mirror for Ministers through the Ages (Lidai chenjian), carrying encouragement and admonition for all who serve as ministers and sons to the utmost. Can you expound and extol those broad principles and essential meanings in these books that illuminate one another? You examination candidates will soon serve in office, extending your filial piety into loyalty. Moreover, you personally encounter the beginning of the present emperor’s reign, precisely the time for ministers and sons to exert themselves. I ask you to set down in writing what you have long studied and understood, so that we may discern how you will render effective service in the future.
Question: The flourishing of talent has commonly depended upon the way of government. Throughout this land of Jin, during the flourishing ages of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties, there were many accomplished and cultivated men who upheld virtue and established meritorious achievements, lofty…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
乎不可尚矣春秋而下視古有間然亦
代不乏人試舉表著者言之反周爲唐
與克平淮蔡者其相業相類矣而輔政
元祐與名震契丹者果若是班乎收保
御虜與堅壁困秦者其將略並稱矣而
幕南無庭與峴山立碑者可同日語乎
漆身報主犯難存孤與義不事操者忠
烈同也抑孰爲正弓矢之諫筆正之諫
與力救陸贄者其直言一也果孰爲良
===
一孝友也或居家而善化其族或遇難
而不忘其弟一清節也或保身於亂世
或不屈於治朝作魏晉春秋與敘史記
世家者其史材孰長講學太山視行教
河汾者其經術孰精是皆可比論與抑
孰爲近古與我
國家作人之盛上追隆古其植節宣猷以清
忠亮直炳然爲
先朝重者在三晉果何人與抑亦有理學淵邃
punctuated: 乎不可尚矣。春秋而下，視古有間，然亦代不乏人。試舉表著者言之：反周爲唐與克平淮蔡者，其相業相類矣，而輔政元祐與名震契丹者，果若是班乎？收保御虜與堅壁困秦者，其將略並稱矣，而幕南無庭與峴山立碑者，可同日語乎？漆身報主、犯難存孤與義不事操者，忠烈同也，抑孰爲正？弓矢之諫、筆正之諫與力救陸贄者，其直言一也，果孰爲良？一孝友也，或居家而善化其族，或遇難而不忘其弟；一清節也，或保身於亂世，或不屈於治朝。作《魏晉春秋》與敘《史記》世家者，其史材孰長？講學太山視行教河汾者，其經術孰精？是皆可比論與？抑孰爲近古與？我國家作人之盛，上追隆古，其植節宣猷，以清忠亮直炳然爲先朝重者，在三晉果何人與？抑亦有理學淵邃
translation_en:
…so lofty that they could not be surpassed. From the Spring and Autumn period onward, there was some distance from antiquity, yet no age lacked worthy men. Let us take prominent examples. The man who reversed Zhou’s rule and restored Tang and the man who successfully pacified Huai and Cai were alike in their achievements as chief ministers. But were the man who assisted in governing during the Yuanyou era and the man whose fame awed the Khitan truly of the same rank? The man who secured and defended territory against foreign foes [?] and the man who held firm behind his fortifications and wore down Qin are both celebrated for their generalship. But can the man who left no enemy royal court south of the desert and the man for whom a stele was erected on Mount Xian be discussed on equal terms? The man who lacquered his body to avenge his lord, the man who braved danger to preserve an orphan, and the man who out of righteousness refused to serve Cao Cao shared the same ardent loyalty; yet whose conduct was most correct? The man who remonstrated through bows and arrows, the man who remonstrated about keeping the brush upright, and the man who vigorously sought to save Lu Zhi were alike in speaking frankly; yet whose course was best?

Likewise, in filial devotion and brotherly affection, one remained at home and successfully transformed his clan, while another, encountering danger, did not forget his younger brother. Likewise, in unsullied integrity, one preserved himself in an age of disorder, while another refused to bend even at a well-governed court. Between the author of the Annals of Wei and Jin and the writer of the ‘Hereditary Houses’ in the Records of the Historian, whose talent as a historian was greater? Comparing the man who lectured on Mount Tai with the man who taught in the He–Fen region, whose mastery of the Classics was more profound? Can all these men be assessed comparatively? And which of them came closest to the ancients?

Our dynasty’s flourishing cultivation of talent reaches back to rival high antiquity. Among those who established their integrity and put their counsels into effect, whose purity, loyalty, sincerity, and uprightness shone forth and lent distinction to former reigns, who indeed came from the Three Jin region? And were there also men whose learning in principle was profound…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
而默契聖賢之奧者與其見諸事功果
可以匹古人與諸士景行先哲必有定
論矣請詳言之以觀尚友之學
問財用
國家所急宋臣有言天地生財止有此數不
在官則在民今內外筦庫告匱而閭閻
又多困詘豈其說不足信與抑耗之者
有由而充之者未備也頃者
皇上軫念民貧方下蠲租一
===
詔而邊臣請討甚亟率以爲辭聞之
國初瘡痍甫定蠲
詔凡二十餘下而征討營建諸費視今加多當
時太倉諸邊尚云儲積紅腐未聞有不
足者今承平日久所入視昔非益寡也
何一奉蠲免而遂不足如是耶議者謂
祖宗時屯鹽脩舉故邊餉日充今雖廢壞幾盡
矣獨不可踵而行之與或又謂豪右之
兼幷未復醜虜之內蹂無常屯田卒亦
punctuated:
而默契聖賢之奧者與？其見諸事功，果可以匹古人與？諸士景行先哲，必有定論矣。請詳言之，以觀尚友之學。
問：財用，國家所急。宋臣有言：「天地生財，止有此數，不在官則在民。」今內外筦庫告匱，而閭閻又多困詘，豈其說不足信與？抑耗之者有由，而充之者未備也？頃者，皇上軫念民貧，方下蠲租一詔，而邊臣請討甚亟，率以爲辭。聞之，國初瘡痍甫定，蠲詔凡二十餘下，而征討營建諸費，視今加多。當時太倉、諸邊，尚云儲積紅腐，未聞有不足者。今承平日久，所入視昔非益寡也，何一奉蠲免而遂不足如是耶？議者謂祖宗時屯鹽脩舉，故邊餉日充。今雖廢壞幾盡矣，獨不可踵而行之與？或又謂豪右之兼幷未復，醜虜之內蹂無常，屯田卒亦
translation_en:
…and those who have silently grasped the profound mysteries of the sages and worthies? Can their achievements in practical affairs truly match those of the ancients? You gentlemen admire and emulate the worthy predecessors and surely have reached settled judgments. Please explain these in detail, so that we may assess your learning in taking the ancients as friends.
Question: Financial resources are an urgent concern of the state. A minister of the Song said: “Heaven and earth produce only this fixed quantity of wealth; if it is not held by the government, it is held by the people.” Now treasuries both within the capital and outside it report shortages, while ordinary households also suffer widespread hardship. Is that statement unworthy of belief? Or are there identifiable causes of depletion, while the means of replenishment remain incomplete? Recently, His Majesty, compassionately concerned about the people's poverty, had scarcely issued an edict remitting land taxes when frontier officials began pressing urgently for funds [?], generally citing this as their reason. We have heard that at the founding of the dynasty, when the wounds of warfare had only just begun to heal, more than twenty tax-remission edicts were issued. Yet expenditures on military campaigns and construction exceeded those of today. At that time, grain reserves in the capital's Grand Granary and along the various frontiers were reportedly so abundant that they reddened and rotted; one never heard of shortages. Now, after a long period of peace, revenues are no smaller than formerly. Why should carrying out a single tax remission bring about such shortages?
Those who discuss the matter say that under our imperial ancestors, military agricultural colonies and the salt administration were maintained in good order, so that frontier provisions grew more plentiful by the day. Although these institutions have now fallen almost entirely into disuse and decay, could we not follow the earlier practice and implement it again? Others say that land engrossment by powerful families has not been reversed [?], and that the vile barbarians' incursions and ravages within our borders are unpredictable, so that military agricultural colonies, in the end, also…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
難舉勢要之攬中爲梗私販之橫行靡
禁鹽法遂至不行此豈勢之所趨有不
可復者耶抑有司者爲之而不力也玆
欲使屯鹽並脩官民具足其道何由諸
士子抱當世之慮有槩于中乆矣願悉
言之毋隱
問禦戎無上策自古則然矣顧攘外斯可
以安內要不可諉之無策也是故後之
談邊者若四要四議四策之類在當時
===
皆鑿鑿可行而卒無救于戎患豈其所
談未協時宜罔裨戰守耶抑所行與所
談者悖也今宣大三關密邇胡虜時時
勞我烽燧當事者殫慮宣威攬收羣策
幾無餘蘊矣大抵談守者必曰截險捍
陴虜難長驅也戰無良材可自損重乎
談戰者必曰出奇制勝虜當遠遯也守
多弃野可示積弱乎是二者果不相謀
與抑果孰緩而孰急與說者又謂
punctuated:
難舉，勢要之攬中爲梗，私販之橫行靡禁，鹽法遂至不行。此豈勢之所趨，有不可復者耶？抑有司者爲之而不力也？玆欲使屯鹽並脩，官民具足，其道何由？諸士子抱當世之慮，有槩于中乆矣，願悉言之，毋隱。
問：禦戎無上策，自古則然矣。顧攘外斯可以安內，要不可諉之無策也。是故後之談邊者，若四要、四議、四策之類，在當時皆鑿鑿可行，而卒無救于戎患。豈其所談未協時宜，罔裨戰守耶？抑所行與所談者悖也？今宣大三關密邇胡虜，時時勞我烽燧。當事者殫慮宣威，攬收羣策，幾無餘蘊矣。大抵談守者必曰：「截險捍陴，虜難長驅也。戰無良材，可自損重乎？」談戰者必曰：「出奇制勝，虜當遠遯也。守多弃野，可示積弱乎？」是二者果不相謀與？抑果孰緩而孰急與？說者又謂
translation_en:
…are difficult to establish. Powerful and influential men obstruct the salt system by monopolizing its contracts, while illicit traders operate unchecked; consequently, the salt regulations can no longer be enforced. Is this the inevitable tendency of circumstances, with no possibility of restoration? Or have the responsible officials failed to exert themselves sufficiently? If we now wish to restore both military agricultural colonies and the salt administration, ensuring adequate resources for government and people alike, by what means should we proceed? You examination candidates have long pondered the concerns of the present age and felt deeply about them. Please state your views fully, withholding nothing.
Question: There is no supreme strategy for resisting the Rong: this has been so since antiquity. Yet only by repelling external threats can we secure peace within, and we certainly must not evade responsibility by claiming that no strategy exists. Thus, later discussions of frontier affairs—including such proposals as the Four Essentials, Four Deliberations, and Four Strategies—each seemed eminently practicable in their day, yet ultimately failed to remedy the troubles caused by the Rong. Was this because the proposals did not suit the needs of the time and contributed nothing to fighting or defense? Or did actual practice contradict what had been proposed? Today Xuanfu, Datong, and the Three Passes lie close to the northern invaders, who repeatedly keep our beacon stations busy. Those responsible have exhausted their deliberations, displayed military might, and gathered proposals from all quarters, leaving almost nothing unexplored. Generally, advocates of defense invariably say: “Block the strategic passes and defend the parapets, and the invaders will find it difficult to penetrate far. We lack capable men for battle; can we afford to diminish our own strength?” Advocates of battle invariably say: “Achieve victory through surprise, and the invaders will retreat far away. Defense leaves much open country abandoned; can we afford to display our accumulated weakness?” Are these two approaches truly incompatible? Or which should in fact take lower priority, and which is more urgent? Some commentators further maintain that…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
國初邊制簡嚴所守皆總會要害之處人聚
力完易爲制禦頃因門戶失守堂奥遇
防堡砦日增而衆分戍守日多而力寡
是以聯絡之勢可觀而衰旅之實不足
又不知果爲有見之說否與茲欲規恢
萬全之策以紓
當宁之懷畢竟如何而可子多士生長於斯必
有石畫定見如昔人之協時宜而裨戰
守者矣試吐之以觀爾先憂之志
punctuated: 國初邊制簡嚴，所守皆總會要害之處，人聚力完，易爲制禦。頃因門戶失守，堂奥遇防，堡砦日增而衆分，戍守日多而力寡，是以聯絡之勢可觀，而衰旅之實不足。又不知果爲有見之說否與？茲欲規恢萬全之策，以紓當宁之懷，畢竟如何而可？子多士生長於斯，必有石畫定見，如昔人之協時宜而裨戰守者矣。試吐之，以觀爾先憂之志。
translation_en:
…At the beginning of the dynasty, frontier arrangements were simple and strict. The positions defended were all strategic junctions and vital points; men were concentrated and their strength kept intact, making defense and control easy. Recently, because the gateways were lost, the inner chambers encountered defensive measures [?]. Fortresses and stockades increased daily, dispersing the troops; garrison duties multiplied daily, diminishing their strength. Thus, although the interconnected defenses present an impressive appearance, the weakened forces are in fact inadequate.
Yet is this truly an insightful argument? Now, wishing to devise a comprehensive and foolproof strategy to ease His Majesty’s concerns, what, ultimately, should we do? You candidates were born and raised here and must have firm plans and settled judgments, like those men of old whose proposals suited the needs of their times and benefited both warfare and defense. Set these forth, so that we may see your resolve to take thought for troubles before they arise.

蓋德者治天下之本也德盛而化自神矣非天
象之自然者烏足以擬之夫子有所感而爲當
時告也以爲古之治天下者純任道之治天
下者純任法自夫任法之治行而無爲之化鮮
矣爲治者曷於本焉圖之誠知民不可以徒法
治也而所以率先於上者務求端乎萬化之原
治不可以無本成也而所以敷錫於下者恒懋
建乎維皇之極以正民心一自吾之心得者運
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
子曰：「爲政以德，譬如北辰居其所而衆星共之。」
張四端
同考試官教授徐，批〔本題作者頗多塵語重複，是篇〕〔獨簡切可誦，錄之。〕
考試官教諭王，批〔明暢不滯。〕
考試官教諭劉，批〔透徹。〕

聖人論人君端本之治，而必擬其自然之化焉。蓋德者，治天下之本也。德盛而化自神矣，非天象之自然者，烏足以擬之？夫子有所感而爲當時告也，以爲古之治天下者純任道之治天下者純任法。自夫任法之治行，而無爲之化鮮矣。爲治者曷於本焉圖之？誠知民不可以徒法治也，而所以率先於上者，務求端乎萬化之原；治不可以無本成也，而所以敷錫於下者，恒懋建乎維皇之極。以正民心，一自吾之心得者運
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books

The Master said: “To govern through virtue is like the Pole Star remaining in its place while the multitude of stars pay homage to it.”

Zhang Siduan

Associate Examiner Xu, Professor, comments: “Many who write on this topic use hackneyed expressions and repeat themselves. This essay alone is concise, apt, and worthy of recitation; it is included here.”
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “Clear and fluent, without impediment.”
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “Penetrating and thorough.”

The sage discusses the ruler’s government through setting the root aright, and necessarily likens its transforming influence to the spontaneous workings of nature. For virtue is the root of governing all under Heaven. When virtue flourishes, its transforming influence becomes wondrous of itself. What but the natural workings of the heavens could adequately serve as its likeness? Moved by what he perceived, the Master offered this teaching to his own age. He held that those who governed all under Heaven in antiquity relied entirely on the Way … those who governed all under Heaven relied entirely on laws [?]. Once government relying on laws came into practice, transformation through nonaction became rare. Why do those who govern not direct their efforts toward the root?

Truly understanding that the people cannot be governed by laws alone, in setting an example from above one must strive to rectify the source of all transforming influences. Understanding that good government cannot be achieved without a foundation, in bestowing benefits upon those below one must constantly strive to establish the sovereign’s supreme standard. To rectify the people’s hearts, one puts into operation solely what one has apprehended in one’s own heart …

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
之而不專於法制之尚也以正民行一自吾之
躬行者推之而不恃夫禁令之煩也夫如是吾
知上以德感至治既妙於無爲則下以德應大
化自神於有象擬諸形容不有如北辰居其所
而衆星共之者乎蓋北辰爲天之樞其居有常
尊也初不見其運動之形而衆星麗天之表其
拱有定向也若咸者夫趨附之勢北辰非有期
於衆星也而星之拱極者不外焉天道不言而
成象也人君非有期於庶民也而民之歸德者
===
不外焉聖人無心而成化也是蓋以一人而臨
萬邦人君與北辰同一居尊之體以天下而仰
一人庶民與衆星同一趨向之機天象聖化其
理一而已矣治天下者其亦審所尚也夫抑論
之政者維治之具固不可廢而德者運治之精
尤所當先焉者也春秋之君知有政耳而德則
未之聞也夫子憂之而爲是探本之論他日政
刑德禮之訓尤惓惓焉其意斷可識矣是故禮
樂文章所以懋治也精神心術所以達化也二
punctuated: 之，而不專於法制之尚也；以正民行，一自吾之躬行者推之，而不恃夫禁令之煩也。夫如是，吾知上以德感，至治既妙於無爲，則下以德應，大化自神於有象。擬諸形容，不有如北辰居其所而衆星共之者乎？蓋北辰爲天之樞，其居有常尊也，初不見其運動之形；而衆星麗天之表，其拱有定向也，若咸者夫趨附之勢。北辰非有期於衆星也，而星之拱極者不外焉，天道不言而成象也；人君非有期於庶民也，而民之歸德者不外焉，聖人無心而成化也。是蓋以一人而臨萬邦，人君與北辰同一居尊之體；以天下而仰一人，庶民與衆星同一趨向之機。天象聖化，其理一而已矣。治天下者，其亦審所尚也夫！抑論之，政者維治之具，固不可廢；而德者運治之精，尤所當先焉者也。春秋之君知有政耳，而德則未之聞也。夫子憂之，而爲是探本之論。他日政刑德禮之訓，尤惓惓焉，其意斷可識矣。是故禮樂文章，所以懋治也；精神心術，所以達化也。二
translation_en:
…put it into operation, without exclusively exalting laws and regulations. To rectify the people's conduct, extend to them entirely what I personally practice, without relying on a profusion of prohibitions and commands. If this is done, I know that those above will move others through virtue, and perfect government will attain its subtle efficacy through nonaction; those below will then respond through virtue, and great moral transformation will reveal its wondrous efficacy in visible manifestations. If we sought an image to describe this, would it not resemble the Pole Star remaining in its place while the other stars pay court to it? The Pole Star is the pivot of heaven, occupying a constant position of honor, with no visible sign of movement. The other stars adorn the heavens, turning toward it in a fixed direction, seemingly all drawn to attach themselves to it [?]. The Pole Star has no expectations of the other stars, yet none of those that bow toward the pole departs from it: the Way of Heaven forms its patterns without speaking. The ruler has no expectations of the common people, yet none of those who turn toward his virtue departs from it: the sage brings about transformation without deliberate intent.

Thus, as one person presiding over the myriad states, the ruler shares with the Pole Star the same manner of occupying an exalted position; as all under Heaven look up to one person, the common people share with the other stars the same impulse to turn toward him. The patterns of heaven and the sage's transforming influence operate by one and the same principle. Should not those who govern all under Heaven carefully consider what they exalt? To discuss this further: administrative measures are the instruments that sustain government and certainly cannot be discarded; virtue, however, is the animating essence that sets government in motion, and especially deserves precedence. The rulers of the Spring and Autumn period knew only administrative measures; of virtue they had not yet heard. Concerned about this, the Master offered this discussion probing the root of government. In his teaching on administrative measures, punishments, virtue, and ritual on another occasion, he was especially earnest. His intention can certainly be discerned. Thus ritual, music, and cultural forms serve to advance good government; spiritual vitality and the workings of the mind serve to extend transforming influence. The two…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
者兼脩而不悖萬世治天下之道在是矣君人
者不可以不知
敬大臣也體羣臣也
梁　喬
同考試官教授程　批〔發揮敬體二字明暢無一煩語〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔明順〕
考試官教諭王　批〔清新瑩潤〕
取之
===
人君待臣之道有隆之以禮者有恤之以恩者
蓋大臣羣臣其分不同也隆其禮施其恩而待
之之道各盡矣夫子告魯君以九經之目以爲
君之於臣也不徒有分焉以明其義尤必有道
焉以通其情由家以及朝廷其待臣之道抑何
如誠以調元贊化而師表百寮者有大臣焉所
賴以總理乎天下國家者也不有以敬之則褻
矣是必思其付託之重而所以尊崇之者無不
至焉以隆具瞻之望則信任之專不以疑貳間
其心也以重寅亮之司則寵遇之渥不以叢脞
punctuated:
者兼脩而不悖，萬世治天下之道在是矣。君人者不可以不知。

敬大臣也，體羣臣也。
梁喬
同考試官教授程批〔發揮敬體二字，明暢無一煩語。〕
考試官教諭劉批〔明順。〕
考試官教諭王批〔清新瑩潤。〕
取之。

人君待臣之道，有隆之以禮者，有恤之以恩者。蓋大臣、羣臣，其分不同也。隆其禮，施其恩，而待之之道各盡矣。夫子告魯君以九經之目，以爲君之於臣也，不徒有分焉以明其義，尤必有道焉以通其情。由家以及朝廷，其待臣之道抑何如？誠以調元贊化而師表百寮者，有大臣焉，所賴以總理乎天下國家者也。不有以敬之，則褻矣。是必思其付託之重，而所以尊崇之者無不至焉。以隆具瞻之望，則信任之專，不以疑貳間其心也；以重寅亮之司，則寵遇之渥，不以叢脞
translation_en:
…When both are cultivated together without conflict, herein lies the way to govern all under Heaven for ten thousand generations. Those who rule over others must understand this.

“Respect the great ministers; show sympathetic consideration for the body of officials.”
Liang Qiao
Associate Examiner Cheng, Prefectural School Professor, comments: 〔The exposition of the two words ‘respect’ and ‘consideration’ is clear and fluent, without a single superfluous phrase.〕
Examiner Liu, County School Instructor, comments: 〔Clear and coherent.〕
Examiner Wang, County School Instructor, comments: 〔Fresh, lucid, and polished.〕
Accept this essay.

In a ruler’s treatment of his ministers, some are to be exalted through ritual propriety, and others cared for through gracious favor. For the great ministers and the body of officials occupy different stations. By according heightened ritual honors to the former and bestowing favor upon the latter, the ruler fully fulfills the proper way of treating each. When the Master told the ruler of Lu the headings of the nine guiding principles, he held that the ruler’s relationship with his ministers involves more than distinctions of station that clarify their rightful obligations: above all, there must be a way to bring their feelings into mutual accord. From the household to the court, what, then, should his way of treating ministers be?

Indeed, there are great ministers who harmonize the primal forces, assist the work of transformation, and serve as exemplars to all officials. These are the men upon whom the ruler relies for the overall administration of the realm and the state. Without a means of showing them respect, his treatment of them would become irreverent. He must therefore reflect upon the weight of the responsibilities entrusted to them and leave nothing undone in honoring and exalting them. To enhance their prestige as those to whom all look up, he must place undivided trust in them, allowing no suspicion or wavering to estrange their hearts. To dignify their charge of reverently assisting the sovereign, he must treat them with abundant favor, and not, through petty, trifling business …

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
勞其形也蓋名位特亞於一人而晉接自殊於
百辟禮有所當加待大臣之道宜爾也此非九
經之一乎承流宣化而布列庶位者有羣臣焉
所賴以分理乎天下國家者也不有以體之則
睽矣是必念其服事之勤而所以體悉之者無
不周焉以聯手足之愛則推誠以任之不使有
畏沮之心也以弘惠養之恩則設身以處之不
使有俯仰之累也蓋不泥於相懸之分而必察
其相同之心恩有所當施待羣臣之道宜爾也
===
此非九經之一乎是則大臣羣臣莫非立政之
人也敬之體之莫非取人之道也君得臣而萬
化行文武之政尚何患其不舉哉嘗觀先儒胡
氏之言曰人臣爲利祿而效忠則忠必不盡此
可見或敬或體者人君使臣之禮也而無心於
君之敬體者則人臣事君之忠也使一有覬覦
之心雖忠亦私矣故曰無所爲而爲者義也有
所爲而爲者雖義亦利也噫明於此義者而後
可以語純臣之道
punctuated: 勞其形也。蓋名位特亞於一人，而晉接自殊於百辟，禮有所當加，待大臣之道宜爾也。此非九經之一乎？承流宣化而布列庶位者，有羣臣焉，所賴以分理乎天下國家者也。不有以體之，則睽矣。是必念其服事之勤，而所以體悉之者無不周焉。以聯手足之愛，則推誠以任之，不使有畏沮之心也；以弘惠養之恩，則設身以處之，不使有俯仰之累也。蓋不泥於相懸之分，而必察其相同之心，恩有所當施，待羣臣之道宜爾也。此非九經之一乎？是則大臣羣臣，莫非立政之人也；敬之體之，莫非取人之道也。君得臣而萬化行，文武之政，尚何患其不舉哉？嘗觀先儒胡氏之言曰：「人臣爲利祿而效忠，則忠必不盡。」此可見，或敬或體者，人君使臣之禮也；而無心於君之敬體者，則人臣事君之忠也。使一有覬覦之心，雖忠亦私矣。故曰：「無所爲而爲者，義也；有所爲而爲者，雖義亦利也。」噫！明於此義者，而後可以語純臣之道。
translation_en:
…burden their bodies with petty business. Their rank and standing are second only to the ruler himself, and their reception in audience naturally differs from that of the other officials. Where greater ceremonial respect is due, it must be accorded: such is the proper way to treat great ministers. Is this not one of the nine guiding principles?

Among those who carry forward the ruler’s influence, spread his transforming instruction, and occupy the various offices are the body of officials, upon whom he relies to share in governing the realm and the state. Unless he treats them with sympathetic understanding, estrangement will arise. He must therefore consider their diligence in service and be thorough in understanding their circumstances. To strengthen the affection that binds them to him like hands and feet, he must entrust them with responsibilities in complete sincerity, allowing them no cause for fear or discouragement. To extend his beneficence in caring for them, he must put himself in their place when dealing with them, allowing them no burdens in supporting their households. He must not be bound by the great disparity in their respective stations, but must recognize the feelings they share. Where kindness is due, it must be bestowed: such is the proper way to treat the body of officials. Is this not one of the nine guiding principles?

Thus, great ministers and the body of officials alike are men through whom government is established; respecting the former and sympathetically understanding the latter are both ways of securing worthy men. When the ruler obtains such ministers, every transforming influence takes effect. Why then should he worry that the government of Kings Wen and Wu cannot be put into practice?

I have read these words of the earlier Confucian scholar Hu: “If a minister renders loyal service for profit and emolument, his loyalty will necessarily fall short of completeness.” From this we can see that respect and sympathetic understanding constitute the ritual propriety with which a ruler employs his ministers, while serving without thought of the ruler’s respect or sympathetic understanding constitutes the loyalty with which a minister serves his ruler. Once any desire for personal gain enters his heart, even his loyalty becomes self-serving. Thus it is said: “To act without an ulterior purpose is righteousness; to act with an ulterior purpose, even when the act is righteous, is still the pursuit of profit.” Ah! Only with an understanding of this principle can one discuss the way of a minister whose devotion is pure.

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
及其聞一善言見一善行若決江河沛然
莫之能禦也
郭之屏
同考試官教授張　批〔形容大舜應善處言有根據與諸作迥別宜式多士〕
考試官教諭王　批〔思致超脫不羣〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔典雅〕
聖人之於善有所感而應之速也夫聖人心通
天下之善者也有弗感感卽通矣非大舜其孰
===
能之孟子知舜之深故言此若曰舜之爲聖也
萬理畢具者虛明之體隨感而應者樂善之眞
方其深山之居所以無異於野人者特以其未
有所感焉耳故及其好問好察之下一言之善
或得於所聞焉明目達聰之餘一行之善或得
於所見焉將見言方入於耳也理卽悟於心也
樂而取之無凝滯也行方接於目也善卽契於
中也舍而從之無勉彊也濬哲之淵涵觸機而
自動一言之善者通其感則以明庶物以察人
punctuated:
及其聞一善言，見一善行，若決江河，沛然莫之能禦也。

郭之屏

同考試官教授張　批〔形容大舜應善處，言有根據，與諸作迥別，宜式多士。〕
考試官教諭王　批〔思致超脫不羣。〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔典雅。〕

聖人之於善，有所感而應之速也。夫聖人，心通天下之善者也。有弗感，感卽通矣，非大舜其孰能之？孟子知舜之深，故言此。若曰：舜之爲聖也，萬理畢具者，虛明之體；隨感而應者，樂善之眞。方其深山之居，所以無異於野人者，特以其未有所感焉耳。故及其好問好察之下，一言之善或得於所聞焉；明目達聰之餘，一行之善或得於所見焉。將見言方入於耳也，理卽悟於心也，樂而取之，無凝滯也；行方接於目也，善卽契於中也，舍而從之，無勉彊也。濬哲之淵涵，觸機而自動，一言之善者通其感，則以明庶物，以察人
translation_en:
“When he heard a single good saying or saw a single good deed, he was like the Yangzi or Yellow River bursting its banks, surging forth with a force that nothing could withstand.”

Guo Zhiping

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: 〔In depicting how the great Shun responded to goodness, his words have a firm basis. This stands distinctly apart from the other compositions and should serve as a model for the candidates.〕
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: 〔The conception rises above the ordinary and stands apart from the crowd.〕
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: 〔Classical and elegant.〕

When the sage encounters goodness, something stirs him and he responds swiftly. For the sage is one whose mind is open to all the goodness under Heaven. There may be occasions when nothing stirs him; once stirred, however, he immediately comprehends. Who but the great Shun could achieve this? Mencius understood Shun profoundly, and therefore spoke these words. It is as though he were saying: in Shun’s sageliness, the complete presence of all principles constituted the open and luminous substance of his mind; his response to every stimulus expressed his genuine delight in goodness.

When he dwelt deep in the mountains, the reason he was no different from a rustic was simply that he had not yet encountered anything to stir him. Thus, through his fondness for questioning and examining, he might discover a good saying in what he heard; through keeping his sight keen and his hearing receptive, he might discover a good deed in what he saw. One would then see that, as soon as the saying entered his ears, its principle was understood in his mind: he delighted in it and adopted it without hesitation. As soon as the deed met his eyes, its goodness found accord within him: he set aside his own way and followed it, without forcing himself.

The deep reservoir of his penetrating wisdom moved of itself when touched by a stimulus. When the goodness of a single saying awakened his understanding, he thereby illuminated the myriad things and examined human …

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
倫將無思而無不通矣卽其孚感之妙不猶江
河之決而沛然莫禦者乎文明之內蘊逢源而
自達一行之善者協於衷則仁由此行義由此
出將不疾而無不速矣卽其順應之神不猶江
河之決而就下莫過者乎是蓋理之藏於中也
與江河之積者同其深故善之應於外也與江
河之決者同其順此固舜之弗可及者也豈獨
異於深山之野人已哉抑舜自耕稼陶漁以至
爲帝無非取諸人者夫舜旣聖人矣善無不足
===
矣而猶不自用焉故其心之虛者益虛明者益
明而應善之所以神也不然淺中而狹外舜亦
猶夫人爾惡乎神然則君子之憂欲如舜者亦
曰勉彊好善焉可矣
易
乾元者始而亨者也
張四端
同考試官教授徐　批〔發揮始則必亨處詞明理達似可與言化機者取之〕
punctuated:
倫，將無思而無不通矣。卽其孚感之妙，不猶江河之決而沛然莫禦者乎？文明之內蘊，逢源而自達；一行之善者協於衷，則仁由此行，義由此出，將不疾而無不速矣。卽其順應之神，不猶江河之決而就下莫過者乎？是蓋理之藏於中也，與江河之積者同其深；故善之應於外也，與江河之決者同其順。此固舜之弗可及者也，豈獨異於深山之野人已哉？抑舜自耕稼陶漁以至爲帝，無非取諸人者。夫舜旣聖人矣，善無不足矣，而猶不自用焉。故其心之虛者益虛，明者益明，而應善之所以神也。不然，淺中而狹外，舜亦猶夫人爾，惡乎神？然則君子之憂欲如舜者，亦曰勉彊好善焉可矣。
易
乾元者，始而亨者也。
張四端
同考試官教授徐　批〔發揮始則必亨處，詞明理達，似可與言化機者，取之。〕
translation_en:
…human relationships: without deliberation, there would be nothing he did not comprehend. Is not the subtle efficacy of his sincere responsiveness like the bursting forth of the Yangzi and Yellow rivers, surging irresistibly onward? The cultivated brilliance stored within him flows forth of itself upon finding its source. When the goodness of a single deed accords with his innermost heart, benevolence is practiced through it and righteousness proceeds from it; without haste, nothing fails to be accomplished swiftly. Is not the wondrous efficacy of his fitting response like the bursting forth of the Yangzi and Yellow rivers, unsurpassed in their downward flow? Thus, principle stored within him shares the depth of the accumulated waters of those rivers; goodness responding outwardly shares the unhindered flow of their released waters. This is indeed what makes Shun impossible to equal. How could he merely have differed from the rustic inhabitants of the remote mountains? Moreover, from his days of plowing, planting, making pottery, and fishing until he became emperor, Shun invariably drew upon others. Though already a sage, lacking nothing in goodness, he still did not rely solely on his own judgment. Hence the openness of his mind became ever more open, and its clarity ever clearer: this explains the wondrous efficacy of his responsiveness to goodness. Otherwise, shallow within and narrow in his dealings with the outside world, Shun would have been just like any ordinary person. Where would his wondrous efficacy have lain? Thus, for the gentleman whose concern is to become like Shun [?], it is enough simply to strive diligently to delight in goodness.

Book of Changes

“The primal power of Qian is that which initiates and brings to fruition.”

Zhang Siduan

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, a Confucian School Professor: 〔He develops the point that initiation necessarily leads to fruition. His language is clear and his reasoning lucid; he seems someone with whom one could discuss the workings of transformation. Accept him.〕

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭王　批〔詞氣　豐達〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔明　當〕
乾元之爲德始物而必通者也夫物必得始而
後生也乾元既有以始物矣而亨則惡可已哉
今夫乾卽天也而元則天德之首也天德不可
言而化機爲可見故欲識乾元者亦驗諸物焉
已矣蓋方天道之靜而未動也則萬物固未有
其始而亦何有於亨也惟夫乾之爲元也鼓大
造於微茫而一理之方出者有以立羣生之命
===
顯神功於本動而一氣之方行者有以開萬化
之先而物於是乎有始矣始則朕兆既萌而生
意之自無而有者必自有而著品彙於是乎咸
章也機緘一啓而元化之由靜而動者必由動
而變庶類於是乎潔齊也理既有以始其性而
理之出也不可止息則繼善之後成性者必達
焉沛然大用之顯行若有神以運之而不容自
已者矣氣既有以始其形而氣之行也自無閒
斷則見象之後形器者必通焉燦然全體之呈
punctuated:
考試官教諭王　批〔詞氣　豐達〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔明　當〕
乾元之爲德，始物而必通者也。夫物必得始而後生也，乾元既有以始物矣，而亨則惡可已哉？今夫乾卽天也，而元則天德之首也。天德不可言，而化機爲可見，故欲識乾元者，亦驗諸物焉已矣。蓋方天道之靜而未動也，則萬物固未有其始，而亦何有於亨也？惟夫乾之爲元也，鼓大造於微茫，而一理之方出者有以立羣生之命；顯神功於本動，而一氣之方行者有以開萬化之先，而物於是乎有始矣。始則朕兆既萌，而生意之自無而有者必自有而著，品彙於是乎咸章也；機緘一啓，而元化之由靜而動者必由動而變，庶類於是乎潔齊也。理既有以始其性，而理之出也不可止息，則繼善之後，成性者必達焉。沛然大用之顯行，若有神以運之而不容自已者矣。氣既有以始其形，而氣之行也自無閒斷，則見象之後，形器者必通焉。燦然全體之呈
translation_en:
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔The diction and tenor are ample and fluent.〕
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔Clear and apt.〕
The virtue of Qian’s origination (yuan) is to give things their beginning and necessarily bring them to fulfillment. Things must receive a beginning before they can come into being. Once Qian’s origination has given things their beginning, how could their flourishing (heng) be halted? Qian is Heaven, and origination is foremost among Heaven’s virtues. Heaven’s virtue cannot be expressed in words, but the workings of transformation can be observed. Thus, whoever wishes to understand Qian’s origination need only examine it in things.
When the Way of Heaven is still and has not yet moved, the myriad things have not yet had their beginning: how, then, could there be any flourishing? It is precisely through Qian’s origination that the great creative process is set in motion amid the faint and indistinct. The one principle, just emerging, establishes the allotted existence of all living beings. Its wondrous efficacy is manifested in primal movement [?], and the one vital force (qi), just beginning to circulate, initiates the myriad transformations. Thus things acquire their beginning.
Once they begin, their first signs have sprouted; the impulse of life, passing from nonexistence into existence, must pass from existence into manifest expression. Thus all categories of things become apparent. Once the mechanism is set in motion, primordial transformation, passing from stillness into movement, must pass from movement into change. Thus the many kinds of beings become fully and evenly arrayed. Principle has already initiated their natures, and its emergence cannot cease; hence, after the continuation that is goodness, the completion that is individual nature must attain full expression. Abundantly, its great operation proceeds visibly, as though some spiritual power were directing it, allowing it no respite. Vital force has already initiated their forms, and its circulation is inherently uninterrupted; hence, after images appear, concrete forms must attain full development. Resplendently, the entire substance displays …

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
靈若有機以使之而不可或禦禦者矣是蓋一元
未始之先則日新之德藏諸用雖欲亨焉而不
可得也一元既始之後則富有之業顯諸仁雖
欲不亨焉亦不可得也信乎物之始者元以始
之而亨者亦元以亨之矣乾元之德不從可識
哉抑此可以見君德也蓋天之亨萬物也始於
元而聖人之亨萬民也始於仁是故萬邦協和
如天之仁始之也四方風動好生之仁始之也
始則必亨聖人與昊天同一道矣而仁又始於
純心也一念之誠僞少殊而王伯從之矣是故
君心不可不愼其始
===
易其至矣乎夫易聖人所以崇德而廣業
也知崇禮卑崇效天卑法地
秦希相
同考試官教授徐　批　通篇簡潔講知崇禮卑處尤精
殆學易而有得者
考試官教諭王　批　語精意到
考試官教諭劉　批　潔淨之文
punctuated:
靈，若有機以使之而不可或禦禦者矣。是蓋一元未始之先，則日新之德藏諸用，雖欲亨焉而不可得也；一元既始之後，則富有之業顯諸仁，雖欲不亨焉亦不可得也。信乎，物之始者，元以始之，而亨者，亦元以亨之矣。乾元之德，不從可識哉？抑此可以見君德也。蓋天之亨萬物也始於元，而聖人之亨萬民也始於仁。是故萬邦協和，如天之仁始之也；四方風動，好生之仁始之也。始則必亨，聖人與昊天同一道矣。而仁又始於純心也。一念之誠僞少殊，而王伯從之矣。是故君心不可不愼其始。

《易》，其至矣乎！夫《易》，聖人所以崇德而廣業也。知崇禮卑，崇效天，卑法地。

秦希相

同考試官教授徐，批：通篇簡潔，講知崇禮卑處尤精，殆學《易》而有得者。

考試官教諭王，批：語精意到。

考試官教諭劉，批：潔淨之文。
translation_en:
…its numinous efficacy, as though some mechanism set it in motion and nothing could restrain it [the transcription repeats “restrain”]. Before the inception of the primal origin, the virtue of daily renewal lies concealed in its workings: even if one wished things to flourish, this would be impossible. Once the primal origin has begun, the work of abundant possession manifests itself in benevolence: even if one wished things not to flourish, this too would be impossible. Truly, when things begin, it is the primal origin that initiates them; when they flourish, it is likewise the primal origin that makes them flourish. Can the virtue of Qian’s primal origin not be understood from this [?]?

Here, moreover, we may discern the ruler’s virtue. Heaven’s causing the myriad things to flourish begins with the primal origin; the sage’s causing the myriad people to flourish begins with benevolence. Thus, when the myriad states are brought into concord, benevolence like Heaven’s initiates it; when the four quarters respond as though moved by the wind, benevolence that cherishes life initiates it. Once there is a beginning, flourishing necessarily follows: the sage and August Heaven share one Way. Benevolence, in turn, begins with purity of heart. The slightest difference between sincerity and falsity in a single thought leads respectively to true kingship or hegemony. Therefore, the ruler’s heart must attend carefully to its beginnings.

“The Changes—how consummate it is! The Changes is that by which the sages exalt their virtue and extend their accomplishments. Knowledge is lofty; ritual is lowly. Loftiness emulates Heaven; lowliness models itself on Earth.”

Qin Xixiang.

Associate Examiner Xu, Prefectural Confucian School Professor, comments: “The whole piece is concise and clear. Its discussion of ‘knowledge is lofty; ritual is lowly’ is especially penetrating. Surely its author has gained something from studying the Changes.”

Examiner Wang, County Confucian School Instructor, comments: “The language is precise, and the meaning fully realized.”

Examiner Liu, County Confucian School Instructor, comments: “A piece of pure and clean writing.”

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
大傳贊易道之至必自聖人之盡道者見之也
夫德業同於天地聖人盡道之極也而皆資夫
易焉不可以見易道之至乎吾夫子贊易之意
豈不謂天下惟道爲至而道皆備於易矣易之
爲書也其誠至極而不可加者乎何也蓋天下
之道總諸心者爲德而聖人之德崇不可及矣
然所以崇者易崇之也見諸事者爲業而聖人
之業廣不可限矣然所以廣者易廣之也是故
德莫大於知而易之理乃知之精也聖人於易
===
理而窮之則知來藏往自可通於神明之極矣
知不於是而崇耶業莫要於禮而易之理乃禮
之實也聖人於易理而循之則踐履篤實自有
得於會通之觀矣禮不於是而卑耶夫知惟崇
也則天以峻極而覆萬物於無外聖人以睿知
而統萬理於一心巍然示人以崇者惟天而聖
人若有以效之矣知崇如天而德之崇也爲何
如哉禮惟卑也則地以至順而載萬物於無疆
聖人以敦厚而兼萬善於一體隤然示人以卑
punctuated:
大傳贊易道之至，必自聖人之盡道者見之也。夫德業同於天地，聖人盡道之極也，而皆資夫易焉，不可以見易道之至乎？吾夫子贊易之意，豈不謂天下惟道爲至，而道皆備於易矣？易之爲書也，其誠至極而不可加者乎？何也？蓋天下之道，總諸心者爲德，而聖人之德崇不可及矣，然所以崇者，易崇之也；見諸事者爲業，而聖人之業廣不可限矣，然所以廣者，易廣之也。
是故德莫大於知，而易之理乃知之精也。聖人於易理而窮之，則知來藏往，自可通於神明之極矣，知不於是而崇耶？業莫要於禮，而易之理乃禮之實也。聖人於易理而循之，則踐履篤實，自有得於會通之觀矣，禮不於是而卑耶？
夫知惟崇也，則天以峻極而覆萬物於無外，聖人以睿知而統萬理於一心。巍然示人以崇者惟天，而聖人若有以效之矣。知崇如天，而德之崇也爲何如哉？禮惟卑也，則地以至順而載萬物於無疆，聖人以敦厚而兼萬善於一體。隤然示人以卑
translation_en:
The Great Commentary praises the utmost perfection of the Way of the Changes; this must be discerned through the sage’s complete realization of the Way. For virtue and accomplishment to equal Heaven and Earth is the highest extent of the sage’s realization of the Way, yet both draw upon the Changes. Does this not reveal the utmost perfection of the Way of the Changes? In praising the Changes, did our Master Confucius not mean that, of all things under Heaven, only the Way is supremely perfect, and that the Way is fully contained in the Changes? As a book, is the Changes not truly supremely perfect, admitting of no addition? Why is this so? The Way of all under Heaven, gathered together in the heart, constitutes virtue. The sage’s virtue is so lofty that none can reach it; yet what makes it lofty is the Changes. Manifested in affairs, the Way constitutes accomplishment. The sage’s accomplishment is so broad that it admits of no bounds; yet what broadens it is the Changes.
Thus, nothing in virtue is greater than wisdom, and the principles of the Changes are the essence of wisdom. When the sage thoroughly investigates these principles, he knows what is to come and stores up what has passed, naturally attaining communion with the utmost reaches of spiritual illumination. Does wisdom not thereby become lofty? Nothing is more essential to accomplishment than ritual propriety, and the principles of the Changes are the substance of ritual propriety. When the sage follows these principles, his practice is earnest and substantial, and he naturally gains insight into their interconnected workings. Does ritual propriety not thereby become lowly?
Precisely because wisdom is lofty, Heaven, in its supreme height, covers the myriad things, leaving nothing outside; and the sage, through penetrating wisdom, unites the myriad principles within a single heart. It is Heaven that, towering majestically, displays loftiness to humankind, and the sage seems to have the means to emulate it. When wisdom is lofty like Heaven, how lofty must virtue be! Precisely because ritual propriety is lowly, Earth, through perfect compliance, bears the myriad things without limit; and the sage, through earnestness and generosity, embraces all forms of goodness within his own person. Yieldingly displaying lowliness to humankind …

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
者惟地而聖人若有以法之矣禮卑如地而業
之廣也爲何如哉意德業之崇廣同於天地此
聖人盡道之至也而皆本之易焉則易豈不至
矣乎抑論之太虛同體萬物皆備人心何崇廣
耶惟不以私梏之則高明以極廣大以致而吾
心與天地相似矣於德業又何有焉故學易者
莫先於善事其心以求崇廣之實否則天地法
象也易書麤迹也與吾心不相關矣故曰成性
存存道義之門是爲聖人心易之本也
===
書
在知人在安民
同考試官教授程　批　〔此作深得推廣陳謨之意可取〕
梁喬
考試官教諭王　批　〔詞理明暢〕
考試官教諭劉　批　〔充贍〕
可取
大臣廣陳謨之義惟智仁兼盡而已夫智莫要
於知人仁莫大於安民也大臣陳謨而推及於
punctuated:
者惟地，而聖人若有以法之矣。禮卑如地，而業之廣也爲何如哉！意德業之崇廣同於天地，此聖人盡道之至也，而皆本之易焉，則易豈不至矣乎？抑論之，太虛同體，萬物皆備，人心何崇廣耶！惟不以私梏之，則高明以極，廣大以致，而吾心與天地相似矣。於德業又何有焉？故學易者，莫先於善事其心，以求崇廣之實。否則，天地法象也，易書麤迹也，與吾心不相關矣。故曰：「成性存存，道義之門。」是爲聖人心易之本也。

書
在知人，在安民。

梁喬

考試官教諭劉，批：〔充贍〕

大臣廣陳謨之義，惟智仁兼盡而已。夫智莫要於知人，仁莫大於安民也。大臣陳謨而推及於
translation_en:
…it is Earth alone that manifests lowliness to humankind, and the sage seems to take it as his model. When his ritual propriety is lowly like Earth, how vast must his undertaking be! I consider that attaining loftiness of virtue and breadth of undertaking equal to Heaven and Earth is the ultimate extent to which the sage fulfills the Way. Yet both are rooted in the Changes: is not the Changes, then, supreme? To discuss this further: sharing one substance with the Great Void and containing all things within itself, how lofty and broad is the human heart-mind! If only we do not shackle it with selfishness, its elevation and illumination will reach their utmost, and its breadth and greatness will be fully realized; our heart-mind will then resemble Heaven and Earth. What difficulty will virtue and undertaking present? Thus, for those who study the Changes, nothing takes precedence over tending their heart-mind well, so as to seek the substance of loftiness and breadth. Otherwise, Heaven and Earth are merely models and images, and the book of Changes merely coarse traces, unrelated to our heart-mind. Hence the saying: “Preserving and continually preserving one’s perfected nature is the gateway to the Way and righteousness.” This is the foundation of the sage’s Changes within the heart-mind.

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
此期望其君之意何至哉且其意謂迪德脩身
固人君端本弘化之要矣然由此而究化理之
端以要無窮之治又豈止於是焉已哉何則天
下不能獨治所以分而治之者人也茲者四門
闢矣而賢才至廣寧無遺於濬哲之外者乎是
故在於秉虛明以照臨百官而臧否昭於洞燭
廣耳目以鑒察羣哲而甄別精於大觀德有多
寡綜覈必得其實也任有大小器使必當其可
也夫然則下無遺賢而上無倖位所以布吾迪
===
德之化者益衆矣否則一任之失一職之廢也
而可但已乎民生不能自遂所以奠而安之者
君也茲者九功敘矣而兆民至衆寧無外於好
生之仁者乎是又在於和平以布其政而德惠
周於率土廣博以厚其施而膏澤究於無方以
教萬民必典則敷而使安於敎也以正萬民必
懲勸昭而使若於政也夫然則上無滯惠而下
無困人所以被吾迪德之澤者益廣矣否則一
夫不獲時予之辜也如至治何哉由是而觀古
punctuated: 此，期望其君之意何至哉！且其意謂迪德脩身，固人君端本弘化之要矣。然由此而究化理之端，以要無窮之治，又豈止於是焉已哉？何則？天下不能獨治，所以分而治之者，人也。茲者四門闢矣，而賢才至廣，寧無遺於濬哲之外者乎？是故在於秉虛明以照臨百官，而臧否昭於洞燭；廣耳目以鑒察羣哲，而甄別精於大觀。德有多寡，綜覈必得其實也；任有大小，器使必當其可也。夫然則下無遺賢，而上無倖位，所以布吾迪德之化者益衆矣。否則一任之失，一職之廢也，而可但已乎？民生不能自遂，所以奠而安之者，君也。茲者九功敘矣，而兆民至衆，寧無外於好生之仁者乎？是又在於和平以布其政，而德惠周於率土；廣博以厚其施，而膏澤究於無方。以教萬民，必典則敷而使安於敎也；以正萬民，必懲勸昭而使若於政也。夫然則上無滯惠，而下無困人，所以被吾迪德之澤者益廣矣。否則一夫不獲，時予之辜也，如至治何哉？由是而觀，古
translation_en:
…this: how profound were his hopes for his ruler! His meaning was that practicing virtue and cultivating oneself are indeed essential for a ruler to set the foundation aright and extend his transforming influence. Yet, proceeding from this to pursue the sources of moral transformation and good order, and thereby secure enduring good government, how could one stop here? Why is this so? All under Heaven cannot be governed single-handedly; it is through others that its governance is apportioned and carried out. Now the four gates have been opened, yet worthy and talented men are so numerous: might some still lie beyond the reach of the ruler’s profound discernment? Thus he must maintain an open and discerning mind to oversee the hundred officials, making their merits and failings clear under penetrating scrutiny. He must broaden what he hears and sees to examine the many wise men, distinguishing them precisely through comprehensive observation. Their virtue varies in degree: thorough examination must establish its true measure. Responsibilities vary in magnitude: employing men according to their capacities must fit each to what he can do. Then no worthy man below will be overlooked, and no one above will occupy office through mere good fortune. Those who spread the transforming influence of my practice of virtue will become ever more numerous. Otherwise, a single mistaken appointment means the neglect of an office’s duties. Can one simply leave matters there?

The people cannot secure their livelihoods unaided; it is the ruler who establishes them in security and brings them peace. Now the nine achievements have been set in order, yet the myriad people are so numerous: might some still lie beyond the reach of his life-cherishing benevolence? Thus he must promulgate his government with harmony and equanimity, so that its virtuous bounty reaches every part of the land; he must make his beneficence broad and generous, so that its blessings extend without bounds. To instruct the myriad people, he must disseminate established norms and standards, enabling them to find contentment in his teaching. To rectify the myriad people, he must make punishments and encouragements clear, enabling them to comply with his government. Then no bounty will be withheld above, and no one will remain in distress below. Those who receive the blessings of my practice of virtue will become ever more widespread. Otherwise, if even one man fails to find his proper place, ‘this is my fault.’ How could this accord with perfect government? Viewed in this light, the ancient…

安民仁矣而又欲兼乎智拳拳忠愛無已之情
信非後世可及也哉雖然舜斥四凶而舉元凱
時雍之後風動之化繼焉則知人安民固當時
已致之成效矣何臯陶之謨汲汲焉以望其君
禹且深以爲難若將終不可致者蓋知人安民
固唐虞之治而不能必其知且安者亦天下之
勢也然不委於勢而夫責難之忠於不替則固
禹臯之所以爲臣道之至也孔子曰堯舜其猶
病諸其得虞庭陳謨之心者與
初一日五行次二曰敬用五事
張偉
同考試官教授程　批〔發明五行五事之理真切筆力〕
更健錄之
考試官教諭王　批〔理氣俱到〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔清順〕
===
聖人首第洛書之數而天人之道備焉夫五行
出於天而五事具於人者也聖人第洛書而首
punctuated:
之大臣之望其君也，知人智矣，而又欲兼乎仁；安民仁矣，而又欲兼乎智。拳拳忠愛無已之情，信非後世可及也哉！雖然，舜斥四凶而舉元凱，時雍之後，風動之化繼焉，則知人安民固當時已致之成效矣。何臯陶之謨汲汲焉以望其君，禹且深以爲難，若將終不可致者？蓋知人安民固唐虞之治，而不能必其知且安者，亦天下之勢也。然不委於勢，而夫責難之忠於不替，則固禹臯之所以爲臣道之至也。孔子曰：「堯舜其猶病諸！」其得虞庭陳謨之心者與？

初一日五行，次二曰敬用五事。
張偉
