考試官教諭王批〔理氣俱到〕
考試官教諭劉批〔清順〕

聖人首第洛書之數，而天人之道備焉。夫五行出於天，而五事具於人者也。聖人第洛書而首
translation_en:
…the expectations that the great ministers of antiquity held for their rulers: discerning men was wisdom, yet they wished it to encompass benevolence as well; bringing peace to the people was benevolence, yet they wished it to encompass wisdom as well. Their earnest, unceasing devotion and love truly lay beyond the reach of later generations! Nevertheless, Shun banished the Four Evildoers and raised the Eight Yuan and Eight Kai to office. Once harmony prevailed, his transforming influence followed like the wind. Discerning men and bringing peace to the people were thus achievements already realized at that time. Why, then, did Gao Yao press these expectations upon his ruler so urgently in his counsels, while Yu also regarded them as profoundly difficult, as though they could never be achieved? Discerning men and bringing peace to the people were indeed the substance of government under Yao and Shun; yet the circumstances of the world made it impossible to guarantee either discernment or peace. They nevertheless refused to leave matters to circumstances and never relinquished the loyalty that demanded difficult achievements of their ruler. This was precisely how Yu and Gao Yao brought the way of ministerial service to its highest perfection. Confucius said, “Even Yao and Shun would have found this difficult!” Did he not grasp the spirit in which counsels were presented at Shun’s court?

“First, the Five Phases [?]; second, the reverent use of the Five Activities.”
By Zhang Wei.
Associate Examiner Cheng, a Professor, comments: 〔“The elucidation of the principles of the Five Phases and Five Activities is precise and pertinent; the force of the writing〕 is still more vigorous. Accept it.”
Examiner Wang, an Instructor, comments: 〔“Both principle and vital force are fully addressed.”〕
Examiner Liu, an Instructor, comments: 〔“Clear and fluent.”〕

The sage placed the numbers of the Luo Writing first in order, and therein the Way of Heaven and humanity was complete. The Five Phases issue from Heaven, while the Five Activities are inherent in human beings. In ordering the Luo Writing, the sage placed first…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
茲二者可以觀治道之所先矣箕子告武王之
意以爲因物以呈數者上天佑民之仁因數而
效法者聖人開物之智出書於洛天固啓之矣
禹之敘之者何如是故洛書之數一列於坎數
之始也萬物生於天而五行者乃天道之始也
禹於初一則第之曰五行蓋其化成於陰陽之
變而其運無方利溥於生民之用而其施不匱
剛柔異質而生克相乘所以成造化之能也燥
濕異宜而瀉助相資所以盡曲成之妙也人君
===
以政養萬民而五行之用固天地自然之利矣
其敘之於首者以此與二列於坤一之次也萬
理備於人而五事者乃人道之始也禹於次二
則第之曰敬用五事蓋其質具於天賦而踐形
乃所以盡性秉降於惟皇而愼脩斯可以成身
形色寓乎天則敬以治躬者所以協衆動之宜
也性命通於心思敬以治心者所以善萬物之
理也人君以身正天下而五事之脩固人事當
然之則矣其敘之於二者以此與是則五行天
punctuated: 茲二者，可以觀治道之所先矣。箕子告武王之意，以爲因物以呈數者，上天佑民之仁；因數而效法者，聖人開物之智。出書於洛，天固啓之矣；禹之敘之者何如？是故洛書之數，一列於坎，數之始也。萬物生於天，而五行者乃天道之始也。禹於初一則第之曰五行，蓋其化成於陰陽之變，而其運無方；利溥於生民之用，而其施不匱。剛柔異質，而生克相乘，所以成造化之能也；燥濕異宜，而瀉助相資，所以盡曲成之妙也。人君以政養萬民，而五行之用固天地自然之利矣。其敘之於首者，以此與？二列於坤，一之次也。萬理備於人，而五事者乃人道之始也。禹於次二則第之曰敬用五事，蓋其質具於天賦，而踐形乃所以盡性；秉降於惟皇，而愼脩斯可以成身。形色寓乎天則，敬以治躬者，所以協衆動之宜也；性命通於心思，敬以治心者，所以善萬物之理也。人君以身正天下，而五事之脩固人事當然之則矣。其敘之於二者，以此與？是則五行，天
translation_en:
…these two first, one can discern what takes precedence in the Way of government. The meaning of Jizi’s instruction to King Wu was this: Heaven’s presentation of numbers through a material object expresses its benevolence in protecting the people; the sage’s taking those numbers as a model expresses his wisdom in opening up the potential of things. By bringing forth the Writing of the Luo River, Heaven had indeed provided the revelation. How, then, did Yu arrange it?

Thus, among the numbers of the Luo Writing, one is placed at Kan: it is the beginning of numbers. The myriad things arise from Heaven, and the Five Phases are the beginning of Heaven’s Way. Under “first, one,” Yu accordingly ranked the Five Phases. Their transformations are accomplished through the changes of yin and yang, and their operation has no fixed bounds; their benefits extend widely to the needs of the people, and their provision is inexhaustible. Hard and soft differ in substance, yet generation and conquest act upon one another, thereby realizing the powers of creation and transformation. Dry and wet differ in what suits them, yet draining and assisting complement one another, thereby fully realizing the subtle efficacy of bringing each thing to completion according to its particular nature. The ruler nourishes the myriad people through government, and the operation of the Five Phases is indeed the benefit naturally provided by Heaven and Earth. Was this not why he placed them first?

Two is placed at Kun: it follows one. The myriad principles are fully present in human beings, and the Five Activities are the beginning of the human Way. Under “next, two,” Yu accordingly ranked “reverently employ the Five Activities.” Their substance is fully present in Heaven’s endowment, and fulfilling one’s bodily form is the means of fully realizing one’s nature; what one holds as one’s endowment descends from the August Sovereign, and through careful cultivation one can perfect oneself. Bodily form and appearance embody Heaven’s standards: reverently governing one’s person is the means of bringing all one’s actions into accord with what is fitting. Nature and destiny communicate with the mind’s thinking: reverently governing the mind is the means of properly realizing the principles of the myriad things. The ruler rectifies all under Heaven through his own person, and cultivation of the Five Activities is indeed the proper standard for human affairs. Was this not why he placed them second? Thus, the Five Phases are Heaven’s…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
道也用於人者也五事入道也本乎天者也天
人相參治道之大端備矣乎𢡟洛書數也五行
五事理也聖人因數而參之以理所以紹天心
明治法也人君能得乎此則五行脩而王道備
五事脩而治本端天下可不勞而治矣漢儒道
術不明乃以陰陽牽合附會隨使為治者目為
象數之末忽而不講禹之心於是乎荒矣故善
言箕範者得理而忘數焉可也
詩
我稼既同上入執宮功晝爾于茅宵爾索
綯亟其乘屋其始播百穀
郭之屛
同考試官教授張 批〔邠民相戒治室大要是急於爲〕
農塲中類失輕重獨此作得之宜錄以式
考試官教諭王 批〔善發邠人憂勤之意〕
考試官教諭劉 批〔詞旨明順〕
邠人相戒以治室無非所以爲農也甚矣農事
不可緩也邠人急於治室而惟恐農事之及焉
punctuated:
道也，用於人者也；五事，入道也，本乎天者也。天人相參，治道之大端備矣。乎𢡟！洛書，數也；五行五事，理也。聖人因數而參之以理，所以紹天心、明治法也。人君能得乎此，則五行脩而王道備，五事脩而治本端，天下可不勞而治矣。漢儒道術不明，乃以陰陽牽合附會，隨使為治者目為象數之末，忽而不講，禹之心於是乎荒矣。故善言箕範者，得理而忘數焉，可也。

詩

我稼既同上，入執宮功，晝爾于茅，宵爾索綯，亟其乘屋，其始播百穀。

郭之屛

同考試官教授張批〔邠民相戒治室，大要是急於爲〕農，塲中類失輕重，獨此作得之，宜錄以式。

考試官教諭王批〔善發邠人憂勤之意。〕

考試官教諭劉批〔詞旨明順。〕

邠人相戒以治室，無非所以爲農也。甚矣，農事不可緩也！邠人急於治室，而惟恐農事之及焉。
translation_en:
…the Way of Heaven, applied in human affairs; the Five Activities are the human Way [?], rooted in Heaven. Heaven and humanity complement one another, and the main essentials of the way of government are thus complete. Ah [?]! The Luo Writing concerns numbers; the Five Phases and Five Activities concern principles. The sage takes numbers as his basis and brings principles to bear upon them, thereby carrying forward Heaven’s intent and clarifying the methods of government. If the ruler can grasp this, the Five Phases will be duly ordered and the kingly Way complete; the Five Activities will be cultivated and the foundation of government set right. All under Heaven can then be governed without toil. The Han Confucians did not clearly understand the Way and its methods, but forced connections and strained interpretations through yin and yang. This consequently led those who governed to regard these teachings as mere minutiae of images and numbers, neglecting to study them. Yu’s intent was thereby lost. Thus, those who speak well of Jizi’s Great Plan may grasp its principles and forget its numbers.

Book of Odes

“Our crops have all been gathered”—“above” [?]. “Go in and undertake work on your dwellings. By day gather thatch; by night twist ropes. Hurry up onto the roofs; then begin sowing the hundred grains.”

Guo Zhiping

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, a Prefectural School Professor: 〔The people of Bin urge one another to repair their dwellings; the essential point is their urgency about〕 farming. Candidates in this examination generally misplaced the emphasis. This essay alone gets it right and should be recorded as a model.

Comment by Examiner Wang, a County School Instructor: 〔It aptly brings out the anxious diligence of the people of Bin.〕

Comment by Examiner Liu, a County School Instructor: 〔The wording and meaning are clear and coherent.〕

The people of Bin urge one another to repair their dwellings entirely for the sake of farming. How imperative it is that farm work should not be delayed! The people of Bin hasten to repair their dwellings, fearing only that the season for farm work will overtake them.

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
其憂勤之意可想矣周公陳豳風以告成王至
此蓋謂豳人之於農未甞一日而忘焉者也方
其十月納稼時亦可以少暇矣而其心豈但已
哉其相戒以爲吾人所資以養者稼也而所藉
以居者室也今而百穀用登我稼亦旣同矣邑
居未治宮功其可緩乎故茅以覆宮也晝爾取
之無怠朝焉綯以利用也宵爾索之無怠夕焉
斂於趨事而所以爲旣㳟之圖者慮之無不飭
亟於乘屋而所以爲葺治之計者備之無不周
===
若此者豈吾之棘欲哉蓋天道速於推遷農事
貴於謀始及今不治春且至矣農祥晨正而于
耜之務聿興黍稷重穋又將布之於野矣當此
之時則雖嗣爾股肱猶懼其弗給也而何暇於
治室也哉土膏脉動而舉趾之耕方作禾麻菽
麥又將播之於畝矣當此之時則雖卽爾田功
尚慮其弗逮也而遑及於乘屋也哉由是觀之
其亟於治室者乃所以急於爲農也豳民於農
事信乎不能一日而忘情矣成王其念之乎抑
punctuated: 其憂勤之意可想矣。周公陳豳風以告成王，至此蓋謂豳人之於農，未甞一日而忘焉者也。方其十月納稼時，亦可以少暇矣，而其心豈但已哉？其相戒以爲：「吾人所資以養者稼也，而所藉以居者室也。今而百穀用登，我稼亦旣同矣。邑居未治，宮功其可緩乎？故茅以覆宮也，晝爾取之，無怠朝焉；綯以利用也，宵爾索之，無怠夕焉。斂於趨事，而所以爲旣㳟之圖者，慮之無不飭；亟於乘屋，而所以爲葺治之計者，備之無不周。若此者，豈吾之棘欲哉？蓋天道速於推遷，農事貴於謀始。及今不治，春且至矣。農祥晨正，而于耜之務聿興，黍稷重穋又將布之於野矣。當此之時，則雖嗣爾股肱，猶懼其弗給也，而何暇於治室也哉？土膏脉動，而舉趾之耕方作，禾麻菽麥又將播之於畝矣。當此之時，則雖卽爾田功，尚慮其弗逮也，而遑及於乘屋也哉？」由是觀之，其亟於治室者，乃所以急於爲農也。豳民於農事，信乎不能一日而忘情矣。成王其念之乎？抑
translation_en: …their anxious diligence can well be imagined. When the Duke of Zhou set forth the Airs of Bin to admonish King Cheng, his meaning at this point was surely that the people of Bin never let a single day pass without thinking of farming. When they brought in their crops in the tenth month, they might have enjoyed a little leisure; yet how could their minds simply rest? They admonished one another, saying: “What sustains us is our crops; what shelters us is our houses. Now the various grains have ripened, and our harvest has all been gathered. If our dwellings have not been put in order, can work on our houses be delayed? Thatch is needed to cover the houses: gather it by day, wasting no morning. Rope is needed for use in the work: twist it by night, wasting no evening. Apply yourselves diligently to the tasks, arranging every detail of the plan for completing the houses [?]; hasten to climb onto the roofs, making thorough preparations for their repair. Is such conduct merely our own impatient desire? The seasons swiftly succeed one another, and farming requires planning at the outset. Unless we make repairs now, spring will soon be here. When the farmer’s star stands due south at dawn, the work with ploughshares will begin, and millet of different kinds, both late- and early-ripening, must again be sown in the fields. At that time, even if you keep your limbs constantly at work, you will still fear that your efforts are insufficient. What leisure will you have to repair your houses? When the fertile earth begins to stir, ploughing will get under way, and grain, hemp, beans, and wheat must again be sown in the plots. At that time, even if you devote yourselves to fieldwork, you will still fear that you cannot keep up. How could you find time to climb onto the roofs?” Viewed in this light, their haste to repair their houses was precisely an expression of their urgency about farming. Truly, the people of Bin could not let a single day pass without concern for agricultural work. Will King Cheng take this to heart? Or…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
周家以農事開國若后稷之稼穡文王之田功
武王之重民食固有周家法也以周公之忠乃
於豳風無逸惓惓爲成王告者豈非欲法祖德
而知小人之依乎厥後成王有昭假之命臣工
之戒卒爲有周令主者孰非周公訓迪之力也
故稱成周之治者頌周公之功不衰
永言孝思昭哉嗣服
高崧
同考試官教授張　批〔是題本人心以徵聖孝而繼先之業因之義本精邃場中作者類多離繞可厭是篇發明清透而詞〕
===
考試官教諭王　批〔意明詞確〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔典雅可觀〕
〔采煥然可以言詩矣〕
詩人徵聖孝之純而贊其光先業焉夫孝者大
化之本也聖孝極其純矣則於先業不有光哉
詩人美武王之纘緒至此蓋曰大哉孝之道乎
帝王之所以上承祖業下孚人心者也使孝有
未純則無以啓人心之應而繼先之業弗彰矣
punctuated:
周家以農事開國，若后稷之稼穡、文王之田功、武王之重民食，固有周家法也。以周公之忠，乃於《豳風》《無逸》惓惓爲成王告者，豈非欲法祖德而知小人之依乎？厥後成王有《昭假》之命、《臣工》之戒，卒爲有周令主者，孰非周公訓迪之力也？故稱成周之治者，頌周公之功不衰。

永言孝思，昭哉嗣服。
高崧
同考試官教授張批〔是題本人心以徵聖孝，而繼先之業因之，義本精邃。場中作者類多離繞可厭。是篇發明清透，而詞〕
考試官教諭王批〔意明詞確。〕
考試官教諭劉批〔典雅可觀。〕
〔采煥然，可以言詩矣。〕

詩人徵聖孝之純，而贊其光先業焉。夫孝者，大化之本也。聖孝極其純矣，則於先業不有光哉？詩人美武王之纘緒，至此蓋曰：大哉，孝之道乎！帝王之所以上承祖業，下孚人心者也。使孝有未純，則無以啓人心之應，而繼先之業弗彰矣。
translation_en:
…The house of Zhou founded its state upon agriculture. Hou Ji’s sowing and reaping, King Wen’s work in the fields, and King Wu’s concern for the people’s food were indeed established traditions of the Zhou house. With all his loyalty, the Duke of Zhou earnestly instructed King Cheng through the Airs of Bin and Against Idleness. Was this not because he wished him to emulate his ancestors’ virtue and understand what the common people depended upon? Later, King Cheng issued the charge concerning “Zhaojia” [?] and the admonition in Ministerial Officers, ultimately becoming an excellent ruler of Zhou. What part of this did not owe itself to the Duke of Zhou’s instruction and guidance? Thus those who praise the good government of Zhou continue undiminished in their celebration of the Duke of Zhou’s achievements.

“Ever mindful of filial devotion, illustriously he took up his inherited charge.”
Gao Song

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Professor: 〔This topic takes the human heart as the basis for demonstrating the sage’s filial devotion; his continuation of his predecessors’ undertaking follows from this. Its meaning is inherently subtle and profound. Most candidates’ treatments stray from the subject and wind about tediously. This essay elucidates it clearly and thoroughly, while its literary…〕
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: 〔The meaning is clear and the wording precise.〕
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: 〔Classically elegant and worthy of appreciation.〕
〔…brilliance shines forth: here is someone qualified to discuss the Poetry.〕 [Continuation of Zhang’s comment.]

The poet demonstrates the purity of the sage’s filial devotion and praises the lustre he thereby lends to his predecessors’ undertaking. Filial devotion is the foundation of great moral transformation. When the sage’s filial devotion attains perfect purity, does it not lend lustre to his predecessors’ undertaking? Here, in praising King Wu’s continuation of the ancestral line, the poet is in effect saying: Great indeed is the Way of filial devotion! Through it, emperors and kings uphold their ancestors’ undertaking above and win the trust of the people’s hearts below. If filial devotion falls short of purity, it cannot awaken a response in the people’s hearts, and the undertaking of continuing one’s predecessors’ work will fail to shine forth.…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
今以天下應武王是其能敦罔極之懷而思以
繼其志者存存而匪懈隆不匱之誠而思以述
其事者亹亹而不忘世德之求不始勤而終怠
也理不息而此心之奉乎理者亦不息殆與先
德之貽相爲悠久矣天命之配不暫合而遽離
也道不已而此心之體乎道者亦不已殆與於
穆之運相爲循環矣此固武王孝心之純也不
有以爲繼緒之光乎蓋先王創其業於前莫不
欲大其業於後也茲合天下以成其孝則光訓
===
對揚而嗣續之圖有以炳燿於天下令德光昭
而纘承之緒有以丕著於人心求清之治視之
肇基其勤者而益彰祖烈重熙炳乎天地爲昭
矣一統之業質之三分有二者而益大文謨丕
顯燦乎日月同明矣是則以一人之孝而光先
王之業此之謂天子之孝也所以配三后於鎬
京者不於斯益信哉抑論莫爲於前雖美弗彰
莫爲於後雖盛弗傳有周一代之業非三后之
德固無以成其始而非武王之孝曷克成其終
punctuated: 今以天下應武王，是其能敦罔極之懷，而思以繼其志者存存而匪懈；隆不匱之誠，而思以述其事者亹亹而不忘。世德之求，不始勤而終怠也。理不息，而此心之奉乎理者亦不息，殆與先德之貽相爲悠久矣。天命之配，不暫合而遽離也。道不已，而此心之體乎道者亦不已，殆與於穆之運相爲循環矣。此固武王孝心之純也，不有以爲繼緒之光乎？蓋先王創其業於前，莫不欲大其業於後也。茲合天下以成其孝，則光訓對揚，而嗣續之圖有以炳燿於天下；令德光昭，而纘承之緒有以丕著於人心。求清之治，視之肇基其勤者而益彰，祖烈重熙，炳乎天地爲昭矣；一統之業，質之三分有二者而益大，文謨丕顯，燦乎日月同明矣。是則以一人之孝而光先王之業，此之謂天子之孝也。所以配三后於鎬京者，不於斯益信哉？抑論莫爲於前，雖美弗彰；莫爲於後，雖盛弗傳。有周一代之業，非三后之德，固無以成其始；而非武王之孝，曷克成其終
translation_en:
…Now, the whole realm responded to King Wu: this shows that he could deepen his boundless filial feelings, keeping constantly and tirelessly in mind the resolve to carry on his forebears’ aspirations; and strengthen his inexhaustible sincerity, diligently and unforgettingly seeking to carry forward their deeds. In pursuing the virtue handed down through the generations, he did not begin diligently only to end in indolence. Principle never ceases, and this heart’s devotion to principle likewise never ceases: it endures together with the virtue bequeathed by his ancestors. His accord with Heaven’s Mandate was no momentary union followed by sudden separation. The Way never stops, and this heart’s embodiment of the Way likewise never stops: it moves in continuing cycles together with Heaven’s profound workings. Such indeed was the purity of King Wu’s filial heart. Did it not bring glory to his continuation of the ancestral succession?

When the former kings founded their enterprise, they all wished it to be enlarged by their successors. Now, by uniting the whole realm in the fulfillment of his filial duty, he honored and proclaimed their glorious instructions, making his plans for continuing their work shine throughout the realm. Their excellent virtue shone forth, and the succession he carried forward became manifest in the hearts of the people. His government, seeking purity and order [?], became still more illustrious when compared with those who had labored to lay its foundations; his ancestors’ achievements shone with renewed splendor, radiant throughout Heaven and earth. His achievement of unification became still greater when measured against the possession of two of the realm’s three parts; King Wen’s plans were splendidly realized, shining as brightly as the sun and moon. Thus, through the filial devotion of one man, he brought glory to the enterprise of the former kings. This is what is called the filial devotion of the Son of Heaven. Does this not make still more convincing his worthiness to stand alongside the three ancestral rulers at Haojing?

Moreover, consider this: without someone to act before, even excellence cannot become manifest; without someone to act afterward, even greatness cannot be transmitted. Without the virtue of the three ancestral rulers, the enterprise of the Zhou dynasty could certainly not have been established at its beginning; and without King Wu’s filial devotion, how could it have been brought to completion…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
哉噫上以集三聖未成之統下以開萬世無疆
之業武王之孝信乎其不可及也茲者定爾功
周人所以拳拳於大武之象與故予於是知武
王之有大造於周也
春秋
八月公會齊侯宋公鄭伯曹伯邾人于檉
僖公元年
劉虞夔

春秋紀好予霸主恤內之勤而責望國輔霸之
儔焉此檉之會桓所以致勤於鄭而魯與邾之
好不終則其負桓多矣春秋予奪之也宜哉楚
成君國以來憑陵於鄭甚矣齊桓謀以救鄭於
是合魯與邾而爲檉之會焉春秋曷爲而予齊
也蓋霸業之光啓徼於威武之振揚向者三國
鼓行于元夜遯齊固大申乎安攘之義矣使其
punctuated:
哉！噫！上以集三聖未成之統，下以開萬世無疆之業，武王之孝信乎其不可及也！茲者定爾功，周人所以拳拳於大武之象與？故予於是知武王之有大造於周也。

春秋
八月，公會齊侯、宋公、鄭伯、曹伯、邾人于檉。
僖公元年
劉虞夔

translation_en:
…indeed! Ah! By bringing to completion the succession left unfinished by the three sages before him, and opening the way for an enterprise without limit for ten thousand generations to come, King Wu displayed filial devotion that truly could not be equaled! “Now establish your achievement”: is this why the people of Zhou were so deeply devoted to the representation embodied in the Great Martial Dance? Thus I recognize King Wu’s immense contribution to Zhou.

Spring and Autumn Annals
“In the eighth month, the duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, and a representative of Zhu at Cheng.”
First year of Duke Xi.
Liu Yukui.
Examiner Wang, an Instructor, comments: “This composition bases its argument on approval of Huan and condemnation of Xi. It thoroughly grasps the meaning of the commentary and may serve as a model.”
Examiner Liu, an Instructor, comments: “It captures the Sage’s intent in granting and withholding approval.”

In recording friendly relations, the Spring and Autumn Annals commends the hegemon’s diligence in caring for the states within the realm, while holding the leading states, his partners in supporting the hegemony, to account. This meeting at Cheng was how Huan exerted himself on Zheng’s behalf. Yet the friendship between Lu and Zhu did not endure, and thus they greatly failed Huan. How fitting, then, are the Annals’ judgments of approval and disapproval!

Ever since King Cheng of Chu became ruler of his state, he had gravely oppressed Zheng. Duke Huan of Qi planned to rescue Zheng and therefore brought Lu and Zhu together for the meeting at Cheng. Why do the Annals commend Qi? Because the glorious inauguration of hegemonic rule depends on the assertion of military might. Previously, the three states advanced to Yuan to the beat of drums, and there was a flight by night [?]. title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
有怠心焉則前功之盡隳何以成霸圖耶幸而
桓也酖毒之戒不忘覩暱之憂是急凡所以彌
縫其闕舒鄭人朝夕之急者合列國之君以謀
之無遺策焉卒使孔叔有勤我之思完守老楚
而楚之不能有加於鄭者多此會之有以奪其
氣耳不然鄭其可得寧乎春秋幸諸侯之有桓
而致勤於鄭是以於兹會也予其念之深云曷
爲而罪魯也蓋霸圖之渙散驗於人心之從違
而者幽盟首叛鄭詹來逃魯大失乎安攘之信
===
矣使其能改圖焉則前愆之克蓋將不爲賢君
耶夫何信也久要之誠不篤二三之德猶存凡
所以授策壇坫爲楚人攘却之計者率外飾之
私以應之不由衷焉卒不忍其哀姜之忿楚未
受兵而邾之師徒先告𠛬者多此會之無以約
其心耳不然邾其可爲讎乎春秋深惡叛桓之
有信而忘好於邾是以於兹會也責其爲不誠
云是則予桓者爲鄭計也幸其有霸也惡信者
爲桓計也懼其撓霸也何莫而非世道賴哉雖
punctuated:
有怠心焉，則前功之盡隳，何以成霸圖耶？幸而桓也，酖毒之戒不忘，覩暱之憂是急，凡所以彌縫其闕、舒鄭人朝夕之急者，合列國之君以謀之，無遺策焉。卒使孔叔有勤我之思，完守老楚，而楚之不能有加於鄭者，多此會之有以奪其氣耳。不然，鄭其可得寧乎？春秋幸諸侯之有桓，而致勤於鄭，是以於兹會也，予其念之深云。
曷爲而罪魯也？蓋霸圖之渙散，驗於人心之從違。而者幽盟首叛，鄭詹來逃，魯大失乎安攘之信矣。使其能改圖焉，則前愆之克蓋，將不爲賢君耶？夫何信也，久要之誠不篤，二三之德猶存，凡所以授策壇坫、爲楚人攘却之計者，率外飾之私以應之，不由衷焉。卒不忍其哀姜之忿，楚未受兵，而邾之師徒先告𠛬者，多此會之無以約其心耳。不然，邾其可爲讎乎？春秋深惡叛桓之有信，而忘好於邾，是以於兹會也，責其爲不誠云。
是則予桓者，爲鄭計也，幸其有霸也；惡信者，爲桓計也，懼其撓霸也。何莫而非世道賴哉？雖
translation_en:
…had he become negligent, all his earlier achievements would have been undone: how could he have accomplished his design for hegemony? Fortunately, Duke Huan did not forget the warning against the poison of ease, and urgently addressed the anxiety over growing proximity [?]. In every measure to remedy deficiencies and relieve the pressing distress of the people of Zheng, he assembled the rulers of the various states for deliberation, leaving no expedient unconsidered. Ultimately, he prompted Kong Shu to reflect upon his solicitude for Zheng, maintain its defenses intact, and wear down Chu. Chu’s inability to inflict further harm upon Zheng owed much to this meeting’s having broken its spirit. Otherwise, could Zheng have enjoyed peace? The Spring and Autumn Annals regards it as fortunate that the feudal lords had Duke Huan, who exerted himself for Zheng; thus, in recording this meeting, it commends the depth of his concern.
Why, then, does it condemn Lu? The dissolution of a hegemon’s undertaking is revealed in whether people lend or withhold their allegiance. Previously [?], Lu had been the first to betray the covenant at You, and Zheng Zhan had fled there: Lu had gravely violated its pledge to secure the states and repel outside threats. Had its ruler changed his course and thereby redeemed his earlier faults, would he not have become a worthy lord? Yet Xin [?] lacked steadfast sincerity toward longstanding commitments and remained fickle in conduct. Whenever plans were presented at the covenant assembly to drive back the men of Chu, his responses were governed by a selfish concern for outward appearances, rather than heartfelt conviction. Ultimately, he could not restrain his anger over Ai Jiang. Before Chu had come under attack, the troops of Zhu were the first to suffer punishment. This owed much to the meeting’s failure to bind his heart. Otherwise, could Zhu have become his enemy? The Spring and Autumn Annals deeply abhors Xin [?] for betraying Duke Huan and forgetting his friendship with Zhu; thus, in recording this meeting, it censures his insincerity.
Thus, its commendation of Duke Huan is on Zheng’s behalf: it rejoices that Zheng had a hegemon to protect it. Its condemnation of Xin [?] is on Duke Huan’s behalf: it fears that he would undermine the hegemony. In what respect are these judgments not a support for the moral order of the age? Although…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
然春秋之初未始有霸也而桓創爲之齊之盛
周之衰也况其念深禮謹在於楚人未帖之先
屈完既盟則濤塗見執陽穀之寵樂肆矣鄭安
得不復逃乎聖人之所以致責於僖者亦不得
已救時之弊耳若論其極必夾輔周室進之以
王者之道然後可
宋公陳侯衛侯曹伯會晉師于棐林伐鄭
宣公元年　公會晉師于瓦定公八年
劉貞寬

春秋兩略將兵之霸臣所以示謹權之意也蓋
兵權在君非人臣之所得專者也春秋略盾與
鞅之將謂非所以示謹也哉且夫兵者國之命
也權者兵之維也攬之於君則國昌竊之於臣
則國削不可一日去公室者也聖人恐此義不
明故於晉之趙盾士鞅發之方鄭南附於楚晉
punctuated:
然，春秋之初，未始有霸也，而桓創爲之。齊之盛，周之衰也。况其念深禮謹，在於楚人未帖之先；屈完既盟，則濤塗見執，陽穀之寵樂肆矣，鄭安得不復逃乎？聖人之所以致責於僖者，亦不得已救時之弊耳。若論其極，必夾輔周室，進之以王者之道，然後可。
宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯會晉師于棐林，伐鄭。宣公元年。公會晉師于瓦。定公八年。

translation_en:
…Yet at the beginning of the Spring and Autumn period there had been no hegemon; Duke Huan established that role. Qi’s ascendancy marked Zhou’s decline. Moreover, his profound concern and scrupulous observance of ritual belonged to the time before the people of Chu had been subdued. Once Qu Wan had concluded the covenant, however, Tao Tu was seized, and the indulgence in favor and pleasure at Yanggu became unrestrained [?]. How could Zheng fail to break away again? The Sage’s censure of Duke Xi was likewise an unavoidable response to the abuses of the age. But if we consider the ultimate standard, only by supporting the royal house of Zhou and advancing it through the Way of the true king could one fulfill it.
“The Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao met the army of Jin at Feilin and attacked Zheng.” First year of Duke Xuan. “The duke met the army of Jin at Wa.” Eighth year of Duke Ding.
Liu Zhenkuan.
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “The idea that caution in exercising authority is rooted in rectitude is difficult to elucidate; this composition grasps it.”
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “It also leaves out none of the commentary’s meaning. It should be recorded as a model.”
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “It achieves a careful and rigorous style.”
The Spring and Autumn Annals twice omits the names of ministers commanding the hegemonic state’s troops, thereby conveying the need for caution in exercising authority. Military authority belongs to the ruler; it is not something a subject may monopolize. In omitting Dun and Yang as commanders, could the Spring and Autumn Annals have intended anything other than to teach such caution? Troops are the lifeblood of the state, and authority is what holds troops together. When the ruler retains it, the state flourishes; when a minister usurps it, the state is weakened. It must not leave the ruling house for even a single day. Fearing that this principle would not be understood, the Sage brought it out through the cases of Zhao Dun and Shi Yang of Jin. title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
遣問罪之旅會列國之君於棐林者趙盾也盾
之威固赫然於列辟之上而山河之衆其指揮而
矣不知君盾者有靈焉乾綱總攬於上盾得而
專之耶以聲疑貳之問師之起於伐鄭者非無
名也然惟辟作威實惟靈之所命而盾之將之
者不過盡代終之分爾使兵權上侵而毒衆以
逞其忿則王法之所必禁而豈盾之所得為者
哉故棐林之會而必書晉師者若曰趙盾雖將
要亦與師等也舉師以蔽盾所以見盾之不得
===
專有其民也及齊東侵於魯晉啓救患之師會
魯國之君於瓦亭者士鞅也鞅之德固溢然於
魯國之間而曲沃之師其統馭矣不知君鞅者
有定焉大阿獨持於已鞅得而專之耶以伸急
難之義兵之舉於救魯者非妄動也然惟辟作
福實惟定之所制而鞅之將之者不過效奔走
之勞耳使兵權下移而虐民以行其私則王法
之所必禁而豈鞅之所可犯者哉故瓦之會而
必書晉師者若曰士鞅雖將要亦與師敵也舉
punctuated: 遣問罪之旅，會列國之君於棐林者，趙盾也。盾之威固赫然於列辟之上，而山河之衆，其指揮而矣。不知君盾者有靈焉，乾綱總攬於上，盾得而專之耶？以聲疑貳之問，師之起於伐鄭者，非無名也。然惟辟作威，實惟靈之所命，而盾之將之者，不過盡代終之分爾。使兵權上侵，而毒衆以逞其忿，則王法之所必禁，而豈盾之所得為者哉？故棐林之會而必書晉師者，若曰：「趙盾雖將，要亦與師等也。」舉師以蔽盾，所以見盾之不得專有其民也。及齊東侵於魯，晉啓救患之師，會魯國之君於瓦亭者，士鞅也。鞅之德固溢然於魯國之間，而曲沃之師，其統馭矣。不知君鞅者有定焉，大阿獨持於已，鞅得而專之耶？以伸急難之義，兵之舉於救魯者，非妄動也。然惟辟作福，實惟定之所制，而鞅之將之者，不過效奔走之勞耳。使兵權下移，而虐民以行其私，則王法之所必禁，而豈鞅之所可犯者哉？故瓦之會而必書晉師者，若曰：「士鞅雖將，要亦與師敵也。」舉
translation_en:
…dispatched a punitive force; it was Zhao Dun who assembled the rulers of the various states at Feilin. Dun’s might indeed towered conspicuously above those rulers, and the host from the land of mountains and rivers was at his command [?]. Yet did he not know that he had Duke Ling as his ruler? With sovereign authority held in its entirety by the ruler above, could Dun monopolize it? The army’s campaign against Zheng was not without justification: it proclaimed a charge of wavering allegiance. Yet “only the sovereign may wield punitive power”: the command actually belonged to Duke Ling, while Dun, in leading the army, merely fulfilled his duty to carry his ruler’s undertaking through to completion. If military authority encroached upon the ruler’s power, and Dun harmed the people to gratify his anger, this would necessarily be forbidden by the laws of true kingship. How could it be something Dun was entitled to do? Thus, in recording the meeting at Feilin, the Spring and Autumn Annals invariably writes “the army of Jin,” as if to say: “Although Zhao Dun commanded it, he was ultimately on the same footing as the army.” Naming the army so as to subsume Dun shows that Dun could not claim exclusive possession of its people.

When Qi invaded Lu in the east, Jin mobilized an army to relieve its distress. It was Shi Yang who met the ruler of Lu at Wating. Yang’s beneficence indeed spread abundantly throughout Lu, and the army of Quwo was under his command. Yet did he not know that he had Duke Ding as his ruler? With the great sword of authority held by the ruler alone, could Yang monopolize it? Raising troops to rescue Lu was no rash undertaking: it fulfilled the righteous obligation to aid those in distress. Yet “only the sovereign may bestow blessings”: the decision actually belonged to Duke Ding, while Yang, in leading the army, merely rendered the service of carrying out his orders. If military authority passed down into a subordinate’s hands, and Yang oppressed the people to pursue his private purposes, this would necessarily be forbidden by the laws of true kingship. How could it be a transgression Yang was permitted to commit? Thus, in recording the meeting at Wa, the Spring and Autumn Annals invariably writes “the army of Jin,” as if to say: “Although Shi Yang commanded it, he was ultimately on the same footing as the army.” By mentioning…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
師以徹歎所以見歎之不得擅有乎衆也此義
行則勢無所分天下鮮不忠之臣權有所屬而
其君亦罔不振者矣其斯聖人之心乎抑考田
氏厚施移齊之國季氏盡征奪魯之民其所由
來者漸矣聖人不忍齊魯之禍延於天下故惓
惓然致戒於盾與歎介然趙籍韓虔魏斯亦晉
之三家也卒分晉而爲諸侯是果孰貽之哉聽
會假朝聘之儀重煩移禮樂之柄悼固授之利
器者矣君子謂其有君子之資而未聞學益信

punctuated:
師以徹歎，所以見歎之不得擅有乎衆也。此義行，則勢無所分，天下鮮不忠之臣；權有所屬，而其君亦罔不振者矣。其斯聖人之心乎？抑考田氏厚施移齊之國，季氏盡征奪魯之民，其所由來者漸矣。聖人不忍齊魯之禍延於天下，故惓惓然致戒於盾與歎。介然趙籍、韓虔、魏斯，亦晉之三家也，卒分晉而爲諸侯，是果孰貽之哉？聽會假朝聘之儀，重煩移禮樂之柄，悼固授之利器者矣。君子謂其有君子之資而未聞學，益信。

translation_en:
…By mentioning the army to make clear the position of Tan [?], it shows that Tan could not claim exclusive control over the troops. If this principle prevailed, authority would not be divided, and there would be few disloyal ministers in the world. Power would rest where it belonged, and every ruler would be strengthened. Was this perhaps the sage’s intention? Consider, however, how the Tian lineage, through generous benefactions, appropriated the state of Qi, and how the Ji lineage, by exacting all the levies, took possession of the people of Lu. These developments came about gradually. The sage could not bear to see the calamities of Qi and Lu spread throughout the world, and therefore earnestly admonished Dun and Tan [?; the latter apparently refers to Shi Yang]. Zhao Ji, Han Qian, and Wei Si likewise constituted three houses of Jin; ultimately they partitioned Jin and became feudal lords. Who, indeed, bequeathed this outcome to them? In allowing assemblies, he lent them the ceremonial forms of court audiences and diplomatic visits; through repeated burdens [?], he transferred control over rites and music. Duke Dao was certainly the one who placed these potent instruments in their hands. The gentleman’s judgment that he possessed the qualities of a gentleman but had not received instruction becomes all the more credible.

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
之道陰陽盡之矣達於陰陽而制作之得宜也
不有本乎見於郊特牲者如此蓋曰聖人之制
作固所以洽人道實所以承天道也燕饗之禮
樂得矣而豈無所本哉亦曰樂之來也非自節
奏焉始也蓋由陽氣流行而鼓化機於不息者
有以肇聲氣之元則律呂之相宣於此以發其
秘矣樂其由陽來者乎禮之作也非自節文焉
始也蓋由陰道凝寂而斂庶物於羣分者有以
立秩敘之體則品節之詳明於此以呈其象矣
===
禮其由陰作者乎夫禮樂本於陰陽而使陰陽
不和固無望於禮樂之得矣茲則陽不過亢也
而陰以濟之動靜相乘適得夫闔闢之妙陰不
過肅也而陽以濟之屈伸相感不失乎通復之
常由是樂行於燕饗雖萬有不齊也而異文合
愛莫非節奏之自然優柔平中殆與天地同其
和矣樂有一之弗得哉禮行於燕饗雖萬有不
一也而殊事合敬莫非儀則之當然中正爲觀
固與天地同其節矣禮有一之弗得哉是知陰
punctuated: 之道，陰陽盡之矣。達於陰陽，而制作之得宜也，不有本乎？見於《郊特牲》者如此。蓋曰：聖人之制作，固所以洽人道，實所以承天道也。燕饗之禮樂得矣，而豈無所本哉？亦曰：樂之來也，非自節奏焉始也。蓋由陽氣流行，而鼓化機於不息者，有以肇聲氣之元，則律呂之相宣，於此以發其秘矣。樂其由陽來者乎？禮之作也，非自節文焉始也。蓋由陰道凝寂，而斂庶物於羣分者，有以立秩敘之體，則品節之詳明，於此以呈其象矣。禮其由陰作者乎？夫禮樂本於陰陽，而使陰陽不和，固無望於禮樂之得矣。茲則陽不過亢也，而陰以濟之，動靜相乘，適得夫闔闢之妙；陰不過肅也，而陽以濟之，屈伸相感，不失乎通復之常。由是樂行於燕饗，雖萬有不齊也，而異文合愛，莫非節奏之自然，優柔平中，殆與天地同其和矣。樂有一之弗得哉？禮行於燕饗，雖萬有不一也，而殊事合敬，莫非儀則之當然，中正爲觀，固與天地同其節矣。禮有一之弗得哉？是知陰
translation_en:
…the Way of rites and music is fully encompassed by yin and yang. When one comprehends yin and yang and establishes rites and music appropriately, does this not have a foundation? Such is the account found in “The Single Victim at the Border Sacrifice” (Jiao te sheng). Its meaning is that the sages’ institutions certainly serve to bring harmony to the human Way, but in truth also serve to follow the Way of Heaven. When rites and music at banquets and ceremonial feasts attain their proper form, could they lack a foundation?

One may also say: music does not originate merely in rhythms and beats. Rather, the flowing vital force of yang, ceaselessly driving the workings of transformation, gives rise to the source of sound and vital energy. Through this, the mutually resonating pitch standards reveal their mysteries. Does music not come from yang? The creation of rites does not begin merely with their regulated forms. Rather, the stillness and concentration of the Way of yin, gathering the myriad things into their respective groups, establish the framework of ordered ranks. Through this, the detailed articulation of grades and measures displays its pattern. Do rites not arise from yin?

Rites and music are rooted in yin and yang. Were yin and yang out of harmony, there would certainly be no hope of attaining proper rites and music. Here, however, yang does not become excessively assertive, for yin tempers it. Movement and stillness act upon one another, attaining precisely the subtle workings of closing and opening. Yin does not become excessively austere, for yang tempers it. Contraction and expansion respond to one another, preserving the constant course of circulation and return.

Thus, when music is performed at banquets and ceremonial feasts, although the myriad beings are diverse, their different patterns unite in affection. All express the natural working of rhythms and beats; gentle, unhurried, balanced, and centered, they virtually share the harmony of Heaven and Earth. Could any aspect of music fail to attain its proper realization? When rites are enacted at banquets and ceremonial feasts, although the myriad beings differ, their distinct activities unite in reverence. All accord with the fitting requirements of ceremonial forms and standards; manifesting centrality and correctness, they indeed share the measured order of Heaven and Earth. Could any aspect of rites fail to attain its proper realization? From this we know that yin…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
陽天道也一心具之也禮樂人道也一天爲之
也聖人承天以治人觀制作者當知所本矣雖
然以效法言陰陽肇其端以成功言禮樂終其
用故聖人制禮作樂合乎敬同乎愛卒之天下
之情平而參賛之業畢焉是禮樂所以承天
亦所以賛天矣然則禮樂天之陰陽陰陽人之
禮樂其合而一之者乎故曰不聞性與天道而
言制禮作樂者末也
唯聖人爲能饗帝孝子爲能饗親
吉可久
===
同考試官教授紀　批　聖人格天格親之理是作發明
考試官教諭王　批　詞理俱到
考試官教諭劉　批　得感通之旨
殆盡宜冠本房
記者著仁孝能格乎天親欲人盡祭之義也甚
矣天親之難格也惟仁孝之至者爲能格之欲
祭者尚其盡義也哉記祭義者意謂先王之制
祭祀也所以償鬼神也鬼神無常饗而所以致
punctuated:
陽，天道也，一心具之也；禮樂，人道也，一天爲之也。聖人承天以治人，觀制作者當知所本矣。雖然，以效法言，陰陽肇其端；以成功言，禮樂終其用。故聖人制禮作樂，合乎敬，同乎愛，卒之天下之情平，而參賛之業畢焉。是禮樂所以承天，亦所以賛天矣。然則禮樂，天之陰陽；陰陽，人之禮樂，其合而一之者乎？故曰：「不聞性與天道而言制禮作樂者，末也。」
唯聖人爲能饗帝，孝子爲能饗親。
吉可久
同考試官教授紀批：「聖人格天格親之理，是作發明。」
考試官教諭王批：「詞理俱到。」
考試官教諭劉批：「得感通之旨殆盡，宜冠本房。」
記者著仁孝能格乎天親，欲人盡祭之義也。甚矣，天親之難格也！惟仁孝之至者爲能格之，欲祭者尚其盡義也哉！記祭義者意謂先王之制祭祀也，所以償鬼神也。鬼神無常饗，而所以致
translation_en:
…and yang constitute the Way of Heaven, and a single mind possesses it in full. Ritual and music constitute the human Way, and the one Heaven brings them into being. The sage follows Heaven in governing humanity; those who examine his institutions should understand their foundation. Nevertheless, in terms of taking a model to follow, yin and yang provide the beginning; in terms of bringing the work to completion, ritual and music consummate their operation. Thus the sage establishes ritual and creates music, uniting people in reverence and bringing them together in love. Ultimately, the feelings of all under Heaven are brought into balance, and the work of participating in and assisting Heaven’s transforming activity is completed. Ritual and music thereby both follow Heaven and assist it. Thus ritual and music are Heaven’s yin and yang, while yin and yang are humanity’s ritual and music: are they not united as one? Hence the saying: “To speak of establishing ritual and creating music without having learned about human nature and the Way of Heaven is to concern oneself with mere ramifications.”
“Only a sage can cause the Supreme Lord to accept his offerings; only a filial son can cause his parents to accept his offerings.”
Ji Kejiu
Associate Examiner Ji, a Confucian School Professor, comments: “This composition elucidates the principle by which the sage moves Heaven and his parents.”
Examiner Wang, a Confucian School Instructor, comments: “Both expression and reasoning are fully accomplished.”
Examiner Liu, a Confucian School Instructor, comments: “It grasps almost completely the meaning of spiritual response and communion. It should rank first in this examining section.”
The recorder explains that benevolence and filial devotion can move Heaven and one’s parents, wishing people to fulfill the meaning of sacrifice. How difficult it is to move Heaven and one’s parents! Only those whose benevolence and filial devotion reach perfection can move them. Should not those who wish to offer sacrifices strive to fulfill their meaning? The author of “The Meaning of Sacrifices” means that the former kings instituted sacrifices as a means of recompensing the spirits [?]. The spirits do not invariably accept offerings, and the means by which one brings about…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
其饗者不有待於至人乎是故萬物之生本乎
帝而王者祭帝所以昭事天之仁也自夫仁有
未至而帝之饗也不可必矣惟聖人則奉天理
以周旋而一德之潛孚者既立夫昭事之本故
臨上帝以對越而明德之惟馨者自致夫來格
之神燔柴以升中而精禋達焉天心其不違也
用犢以告虔而休徵應焉天鑒其在茲也蓋雖
天道無常親而惟聖人爲能配天之德則亦惟
聖人爲能承天之既矣帝不饗於聖人而誰饗
===
乎夫人之生本乎親而人子祭親所以致追遠
之孝也自夫孝有未至而親之饗也不可必矣
惟孝子則繼述本於因心而意緒之相承者既
得夫感通之理故禘嘗行於盡制而孝思之融
液者自顯夫如在之誠昭假有廟而精神聚焉
致愛於是乎能存也奏假無言而志意交焉致
慤於是乎能著也蓋雖格思不可度而惟孝子
可以得親之心則亦惟孝子可以爲親之依矣
親不饗於孝子而誰饗乎夫饗帝惟聖則求仁
punctuated: 其饗者，不有待於至人乎？是故萬物之生本乎帝，而王者祭帝，所以昭事天之仁也。自夫仁有未至，而帝之饗也不可必矣。惟聖人則奉天理以周旋，而一德之潛孚者，既立夫昭事之本，故臨上帝以對越，而明德之惟馨者，自致夫來格之神。燔柴以升中，而精禋達焉，天心其不違也；用犢以告虔，而休徵應焉，天鑒其在茲也。蓋雖天道無常親，而惟聖人爲能配天之德，則亦惟聖人爲能承天之既矣。帝不饗於聖人而誰饗乎？夫人之生本乎親，而人子祭親，所以致追遠之孝也。自夫孝有未至，而親之饗也不可必矣。惟孝子則繼述本於因心，而意緒之相承者，既得夫感通之理，故禘嘗行於盡制，而孝思之融液者，自顯夫如在之誠。昭假有廟，而精神聚焉，致愛於是乎能存也；奏假無言，而志意交焉，致慤於是乎能著也。蓋雖格思不可度，而惟孝子可以得親之心，則亦惟孝子可以爲親之依矣。親不饗於孝子而誰饗乎？夫饗帝惟聖，則求仁
translation_en:
…does securing their acceptance of the offerings not depend upon a person of consummate virtue? Thus, the birth of all things has its source in the Supreme Deity, and the king’s sacrifice to the Supreme Deity manifests the benevolence with which he illustriously serves Heaven. If his benevolence falls short of perfection, the Supreme Deity’s acceptance of his offerings cannot be assured. The sage alone follows Heaven’s principle in all his conduct. Through the unseen accord of his undivided virtue, he has already established the foundation for illustrious service. Hence, when he approaches the Supreme Deity in reverent attendance, the fragrance of his luminous virtue naturally brings the spirit to descend. He burns firewood to offer up an account of his achievements, and his pure sacrifice reaches Heaven: Heaven’s heart surely does not oppose him. He offers a calf to declare his reverence, and auspicious signs respond: Heaven’s scrutiny surely rests here. Although Heaven’s Way shows no constant partiality, only the sage can match Heaven’s virtue; thus only the sage can receive Heaven’s favor [?]. If the Supreme Deity does not accept the sage’s offerings, whose offerings will it accept?

Human life has its source in one’s parents, and a son’s sacrifice to his parents expresses the filial devotion of remembering those long departed. If his filial devotion falls short of perfection, his parents’ acceptance of his offerings cannot be assured. Only the filial son grounds his continuation of their purposes and undertakings in the impulses of his own heart. Through the continuity of their intentions and feelings, he has already grasped the principle of spiritual communion. Hence, when he performs the di and chang ancestral sacrifices in full accordance with their prescribed forms, the pervasive flow of his filial thoughts naturally manifests the sincerity with which he treats his parents as present. He illustriously approaches them in the ancestral temple, and their spirits gather there: in this way, the utmost love can preserve their presence. He advances and approaches without words, and their intentions commune: in this way, the utmost sincerity can become manifest. Although the spirits’ coming cannot be fathomed, only the filial son can comprehend his parents’ hearts; thus only the filial son can provide a resting place for their spirits. If his parents do not accept the filial son’s offerings, whose offerings will they accept? Since only the sage can secure the Supreme Deity’s acceptance of offerings, one must seek benevolence…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
於心帝匪遠也饗親惟孝則求孝於心親匪幽
也合仁與孝而饗之義盡矣有祭之責者盍思
諸抑仁孝無二道感通唯一幾故仁人事天如
事親一孝也孝子事親如事天一仁也然則其
實維何曰誠而已誠也者無所爲而爲之心也
必無所爲而後謂之誠必誠而後可以言仁孝
噫是可以觀祭本矣
第貳場
論
===
君道以至誠仁愛爲本
同考試官教授徐　批〔敘云時亭直說人君誠愛之心〕
油然充溢必深於所養者宜錄以式
考試官教諭王　批〔氣格昌大理致精純〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔意正而氣充〕
張四端
論曰君之道天道也天道有本人君體天之心
以盡道亦有本夫天之心何心也至誠無息而
以生物爲心者也君之道何道也以至誠法天
punctuated:
於心，帝匪遠也；饗親惟孝，則求孝於心，親匪幽也。合仁與孝，而饗之義盡矣。有祭之責者盍思諸？抑仁孝無二道，感通唯一幾。故仁人事天如事親，一孝也；孝子事親如事天，一仁也。然則其實維何？曰：誠而已。誠也者，無所爲而爲之心也。必無所爲而後謂之誠，必誠而後可以言仁孝。噫！是可以觀祭本矣。

第貳場
論

君道以至誠仁愛爲本

同考試官教授徐　批〔敘云時亭直說人君誠愛之心〕油然充溢，必深於所養者，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭王　批〔氣格昌大，理致精純〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔意正而氣充〕

張四端

論曰：君之道，天道也。天道有本，人君體天之心以盡道，亦有本。夫天之心何心也？至誠無息，而以生物爲心者也。君之道何道也？以至誠法天
translation_en:
…in the heart, and the Lord on High is not distant. Only filial devotion can bring parents to partake of offerings; seek filial devotion in the heart, and parents are not hidden from us. Together, benevolence and filial devotion encompass the full meaning of their partaking. Should those responsible for sacrifices not reflect on this? Moreover, benevolence and filial devotion are not two distinct ways; spiritual communication and response turn on a single subtle impulse. Thus, the benevolent person serves Heaven as he serves his parents: this is entirely filial devotion. The filial son serves his parents as he serves Heaven: this is entirely benevolence. What, then, is their true substance? Sincerity alone. Sincerity is the disposition to act without an ulterior purpose. Only without an ulterior purpose can one be called sincere; only with sincerity can one speak of benevolence and filial devotion. Ah! Here one may discern the foundation of sacrifice.

Second Session
Discourse

The Way of the Ruler Takes Utmost Sincerity and Benevolent Love as Its Foundation

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Professor: 〔The opening says [?]: it directly explains the ruler’s heart of sincerity and love.〕 It wells up spontaneously and overflows; the writer must have cultivated himself deeply. This should be recorded as a model.
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: 〔Its vigor and style are expansive; its reasoning is refined and pure.〕
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: 〔Its intent is upright and its vigor abundant.〕

The discourse states: The way of the ruler is the Way of Heaven. The Way of Heaven has a foundation; the ruler, embodying Heaven’s heart in order to fulfill the Way, likewise has a foundation. What sort of heart is Heaven’s heart? It is unceasing in utmost sincerity and takes the generation of living things as its purpose. What sort of way is the ruler’s way? It is to emulate Heaven through utmost sincerity…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
而通天下爲一身者也天以生物爲心而本於
至誠故於穆之命流行於萬物而不能以自已
君之爲道亦本於至誠故仁愛之念誕敷於民
物而不容以或忘是故天無私覆人君奉天道
之無私合萬物而囿之以並生並育之化其道
之與天爲一固如此也程子曰君道以至誠仁
愛爲本其知言哉嘗觀諸天地而知人君之治
矣今夫天地之大有一物不在其覆載之中者
乎天下民物之繁有一不賴其生成者乎然上
===
天之載無聲無臭而易之於復則曰復其見天
地之心蓋以羣陰旣盛一陽初生則天命流行
生生不息之意於是乎復萌故以生物爲心者
天地之心也然機緘之妙藏於不言美利之施
溥於無外而太和之保合者本於一誠故中庸
之賛天地曰爲物不貳則其生物不測蓋言不
貳卽誠誠則所以爲天地生物之本也人君之
治天下其尊猶天也居曰天位存曰天德行曰
天道顧不能以其本之誠者徵諸民安在其爲
punctuated: 而通天下爲一身者也。天以生物爲心，而本於至誠，故於穆之命流行於萬物，而不能以自已。君之爲道亦本於至誠，故仁愛之念誕敷於民物，而不容以或忘。是故天無私覆，人君奉天道之無私，合萬物而囿之以並生並育之化，其道之與天爲一，固如此也。程子曰：「君道以至誠仁愛爲本。」其知言哉！嘗觀諸天地，而知人君之治矣。今夫天地之大，有一物不在其覆載之中者乎？天下民物之繁，有一不賴其生成者乎？然上天之載，無聲無臭，而《易》之於復則曰：「復，其見天地之心。」蓋以羣陰旣盛，一陽初生，則天命流行、生生不息之意，於是乎復萌。故以生物爲心者，天地之心也。然機緘之妙藏於不言，美利之施溥於無外，而太和之保合者本於一誠，故《中庸》之賛天地曰：「爲物不貳，則其生物不測。」蓋言不貳卽誠，誠則所以爲天地生物之本也。人君之治天下，其尊猶天也，居曰天位，存曰天德，行曰天道。顧不能以其本之誠者徵諸民，安在其爲
translation_en: …and unite all under Heaven as one body. Heaven takes the generation of living things as its heart, grounded in utmost sincerity; hence its profound and majestic mandate flows through the myriad things without ever ceasing. The ruler’s Way likewise rests on utmost sincerity; hence his concern for benevolence and love extends broadly to the people and all things, never permitting a moment’s forgetfulness. Thus Heaven shelters all without partiality. The ruler upholds the impartiality of Heaven’s Way, gathering the myriad things within a transforming influence that brings them into life and nurtures them together. Such indeed is the unity of his Way with Heaven. Master Cheng said: “The ruler’s Way takes utmost sincerity, benevolence, and love as its foundation.” How well he understood these words! Through observing Heaven and Earth, I have come to understand the ruler’s governance. Vast as Heaven and Earth are, is there any single thing outside their shelter and support? Numerous as the people and things under Heaven are, is there any one that does not depend on them for its generation and completion? Yet “the workings of Heaven above have neither sound nor smell,” while the Book of Changes says of the hexagram Return: “In Return, may we not see the heart of Heaven and Earth?” For when the many yin forces have reached their height and a single yang first arises, the purpose of Heaven’s mandate—flowing onward, generating life without cease—sprouts anew. Thus the heart that takes the generation of living things as its purpose is the heart of Heaven and Earth. Yet the subtle workings of their mechanism lie hidden in silence, and their beneficent gifts extend without limit. The preservation and union of supreme harmony rest upon sincerity alone. Hence the Doctrine of the Mean, in praising Heaven and Earth, says: “In their making of things they are undivided; thus their generation of things is unfathomable.” This means that being undivided is sincerity, and sincerity is the foundation upon which Heaven and Earth generate living things. In governing all under Heaven, the ruler is as exalted as Heaven itself. The position he occupies is called Heaven’s position; what he preserves within is called Heaven’s virtue; what he puts into practice is called Heaven’s Way. Yet if he cannot make the sincerity at their foundation manifest among the people, wherein lies his being…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
天之宗子乎是故必有純天之心而後可以無
忝於所性有憲天之政而後可以無愧於所司
有格天之化而後可以無負於代天理物之寄
故一念之僞非誠也一私之起非仁也一物之
慘非愛也於是以至誠無妄之心擴之爲慈祥
豈弟之政以純一不已之念推之爲博施濟衆
之恩以乾父坤母民胞物與之度達之爲萬物
一體上下同流之化以至海隅蒼生飛潛動植
君有一夫之不得其所一物之不遂其生皆以
===
爲吾心之未盡而惓惓焉思以保護周全之者
蓋未嘗一日忘焉者也若是者豈人君顧爲是
煦煦以徇天下哉蓋君人者體天之心而以天
下爲一身者也以天下爲一身必使元氣周流
靡所不貫何忍坐視其痿痺而不爲之治乎必
使其膏澤淪洽靡所不被何忍坐視其恫瘝而
不爲之恤乎苟治矣恤矣而或揆諸念慮不本
於至誠又何忍矯誣飾私以籠絡天下哉故曰
天以生物爲心而本於至誠人君以法天爲道
punctuated:
天之宗子乎？是故必有純天之心，而後可以無忝於所性；有憲天之政，而後可以無愧於所司；有格天之化，而後可以無負於代天理物之寄。故一念之僞，非誠也；一私之起，非仁也；一物之慘，非愛也。於是以至誠無妄之心，擴之爲慈祥豈弟之政；以純一不已之念，推之爲博施濟衆之恩；以乾父坤母、民胞物與之度，達之爲萬物一體、上下同流之化。以至海隅蒼生、飛潛動植，君有一夫之不得其所、一物之不遂其生，皆以爲吾心之未盡，而惓惓焉思以保護周全之者，蓋未嘗一日忘焉者也。
若是者，豈人君顧爲是煦煦以徇天下哉？蓋君人者體天之心，而以天下爲一身者也。以天下爲一身，必使元氣周流，靡所不貫，何忍坐視其痿痺而不爲之治乎？必使其膏澤淪洽，靡所不被，何忍坐視其恫瘝而不爲之恤乎？苟治矣、恤矣，而或揆諸念慮，不本於至誠，又何忍矯誣飾私以籠絡天下哉？故曰：「天以生物爲心，而本於至誠；人君以法天爲道，
translation_en:
… the principal son of Heaven? Thus, only with a heart wholly aligned with Heaven can he avoid dishonoring his endowed nature; only with government modeled on Heaven can he be free of shame in his charge; and only with a transforming influence that reaches Heaven can he fulfill the trust of ordering all things on Heaven’s behalf. A single false thought is contrary to sincerity; the arising of a single selfish impulse is contrary to benevolence; the suffering of a single creature is contrary to love. He therefore extends a heart of utmost sincerity, free of falsehood, into kindly and gracious government; develops an unwavering, undivided purpose into beneficence that gives widely and aids the multitude; and realizes the breadth of vision that regards Qian as father, Kun as mother, the people as siblings, and all creatures as companions in a transforming influence through which all things form one body and those above and below move in a common current. This extends even to the people at the ocean’s edge, to creatures that fly or swim, and to animals and plants. If the ruler has [?] even one person who has not found a fitting place, or one creature whose life has not reached fulfillment, he considers his own heart’s efforts incomplete. Earnestly concerned, he thinks of how to protect and care fully for them, never forgetting them for a single day.
In acting thus, does the ruler merely dispense petty kindness to please the world? Rather, one who rules embodies Heaven’s heart and regards all under Heaven as a single body. Regarding all under Heaven as a single body, he must ensure that its primal vital energy circulates everywhere, penetrating every part. How could he bear to sit watching its paralysis and numbness without treating them? He must ensure that his nourishing bounty permeates everywhere, leaving nothing untouched. How could he bear to sit watching its pain and suffering without bringing relief? Yet even if he treats and relieves them, should an examination of his thoughts reveal that they are not rooted in utmost sincerity, how could he bear to practice deception and disguise selfish motives in order to win over the world? Thus it is said: “Heaven takes giving life to all things as its heart, rooted in utmost sincerity; the ruler takes emulating Heaven as his Way …

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
而亦本於至誠至誠者其人君仁愛之本乎語
君道而本於至誠是其始也以一人之身愛天
下而不見其不足其既也以天下之大取足於
一人之愛而不見其有餘由是範圍不過曲成
不遺三光我其明之九土我其定之皇極我其
扶植之民彝我其敘正之蓋誠極其至則愛極
其博而與天同運君道蔑以加矣蓋嘗遡而求
之在堯舜則爲如天之仁好生之德而要之允
恭允塞者其本也在禹則爲下車之泣在湯則
===
爲解網之祝而要之祇台彰信者其本也在文
則視民如傷在武則大賚四海而要之緝熙敬
義者其本也彼數聖人者悉以至誠仁愛之心
而措天下於順治後之言君道者必歸焉奈何
三代而下此道不明每以不情之惠假仁愛之
私以欺天下後世而天下信之後世慕之吾恐
帝王仁愛之心固不若是之僞也信乎至誠爲
君道之本求治者其亦審所尚乎雖然誠非可
以徒存也其幾始於窒欲其助在於任賢苟能
punctuated: 而亦本於至誠。至誠者，其人君仁愛之本乎！語君道而本於至誠，是其始也，以一人之身愛天下而不見其不足；其既也，以天下之大取足於一人之愛而不見其有餘。由是範圍不過，曲成不遺。三光，我其明之；九土，我其定之；皇極，我其扶植之；民彝，我其敘正之。蓋誠極其至，則愛極其博，而與天同運，君道蔑以加矣。蓋嘗遡而求之，在堯舜則爲如天之仁、好生之德，而要之允恭允塞者其本也；在禹則爲下車之泣，在湯則爲解網之祝，而要之祇台彰信者其本也；在文則視民如傷，在武則大賚四海，而要之緝熙敬義者其本也。彼數聖人者，悉以至誠仁愛之心而措天下於順治，後之言君道者必歸焉。奈何三代而下，此道不明，每以不情之惠、假仁愛之私，以欺天下後世，而天下信之，後世慕之。吾恐帝王仁愛之心，固不若是之僞也。信乎至誠爲君道之本，求治者其亦審所尚乎！雖然，誠非可以徒存也，其幾始於窒欲，其助在於任賢。苟能
translation_en:
…and likewise takes utmost sincerity as its foundation. Is not utmost sincerity the foundation of a ruler’s benevolent love? When we discuss the ruler’s way and ground it in utmost sincerity, at the outset a single person loves all under Heaven without his love proving insufficient; ultimately, the whole vast realm finds satisfaction in that one person’s love without that love proving excessive. Thus he encompasses all without overstepping and brings each particular thing to fulfillment without omission. The three luminaries—I shall make them shine; the nine regions—I shall bring them stability; the sovereign’s supreme standard—I shall uphold it; the people’s constant moral norms—I shall set them in proper order. When sincerity reaches its utmost, love reaches its widest extent and moves in concert with Heaven. Nothing can surpass this in the ruler’s way.

I have traced this back to its origins. In Yao and Shun it appeared as benevolence like Heaven’s and the virtue of cherishing life; fundamentally, however, genuine reverence and genuine integrity were its basis. In Yu it appeared as his descending from his carriage to weep; in Tang, as his prayer when loosening the hunting nets. Fundamentally, however, reverence and manifest trustworthiness [?] were its basis. King Wen regarded the people as though they were injured; King Wu bestowed great gifts throughout the Four Seas. Fundamentally, however, continuing illumination, reverence, and righteousness were their basis. These several sages all brought the realm into harmonious order through hearts of utmost sincerity and benevolent love. Those who subsequently spoke of the ruler’s way necessarily turned to them.

Why, then, after the Three Dynasties, did this way become obscure? Again and again, men used favors devoid of genuine feeling and self-serving pretenses of benevolent love to deceive the world and later generations. Yet the world believed them, and later generations admired them. I fear that the benevolent hearts of the ancient emperors and kings were surely not so false as this. Truly, utmost sincerity is the foundation of the ruler’s way! Should not those who seek good government carefully examine what they esteem? Nevertheless, sincerity cannot merely be preserved by itself. Its first stirrings begin with restraining desire; its support lies in employing the worthy. If one can…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
閑邪以存誠則明通公溥聖德脩而萬民化矣
用賢以仁身則端本澄源賢才輔而天下治矣
故曰純心要矣用賢急焉君天下者合而觀之
始得

隆慶元年某月某日，恭遇皇上初御經筵，臣等謹上表稱
translation_en:
…ward off evil to preserve sincerity, then understanding will penetrate all things and impartiality extend everywhere; sagely virtue will be cultivated and the myriad people transformed. Employ worthy men to make oneself humane, and the root will be set right and the source purified; worthy talents will assist, and all under Heaven will be well governed. Thus it is said: keeping the heart pure is essential, and employing worthy men is urgent. Only by considering these together can the ruler of all under Heaven grasp the way.

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
賀者
明主大有爲式重正心之學
聖人急先務聿勤論道之思化執維新士林協
慶〔臣〕等誠懽誠忭稽首頓首竊以道心爲
一身之主
君德乃萬化之原惟主敬可以維持此心非典
學曷由懋隆其德虞帝達聰明目績底重
華殷宗學古多聞功昭烈祖周武踐祚之
始即咨敬義之言成王涖政之初載詢緝
===
熙之旨自嬴秦滅學暨炎漢少文彝老臨
雍徒侈儀章之飾執經問難空環觀望之
榮或聚訟以談經或投戈而講藝說書於
麗正愧匪眞知稱制於邇英慚無實用事
如有待道不虛行迨我
皇明爰昭
令典開講筵而晝接賢士類以春融作聖述
明遠紹三王之烈德崇業廣獨宗二帝之
猷試歷數乎前聞竟莫優於
punctuated:
賀者：明主大有爲，式重正心之學；聖人急先務，聿勤論道之思。化執維新，士林協慶。〔臣〕等誠懽誠忭，稽首頓首。
竊以道心爲一身之主，君德乃萬化之原。惟主敬可以維持此心，非典學曷由懋隆其德？虞帝達聰明目，績底重華；殷宗學古多聞，功昭烈祖。周武踐祚之始，即咨敬義之言；成王涖政之初，載詢緝熙之旨。自嬴秦滅學，暨炎漢少文，彝老臨雍，徒侈儀章之飾；執經問難，空環觀望之榮。或聚訟以談經，或投戈而講藝。說書於麗正，愧匪眞知；稱制於邇英，慚無實用。事如有待，道不虛行。
迨我皇明，爰昭令典。開講筵而晝接賢，士類以春融；作聖述明，遠紹三王之烈；德崇業廣，獨宗二帝之猷。試歷數乎前聞，竟莫優於
translation_en:
…to offer congratulations: The enlightened ruler undertakes great deeds and accordingly honors the learning that rectifies the mind; the sage gives priority to what is most urgent and diligently applies his thought to discussing the Way. The work of transformation is renewed [?], and the community of scholars joins in celebration. We, your servants, truly joyful and truly delighted, bow our heads to the ground and repeatedly kowtow.
We humbly consider that the mind of the Way governs the entire person, and the ruler’s virtue is the source of all transformation. Only by making reverence central can this mind be sustained; without constant study, how could his virtue be further exalted? The emperor of Yu opened the channels of hearing and sight, achieving the brilliance that renewed his predecessor’s glory. The ancestral king of Yin studied antiquity and acquired broad learning, his accomplishments illuminating those of his illustrious ancestors. At the beginning of his reign, King Wu of Zhou sought counsel on reverence and righteousness; when King Cheng first assumed government, he inquired into the meaning of continuing and brightening virtue. From the destruction of learning under the Ying house of Qin to the scant cultivation of letters under the fire-associated Han, the elders’ attendance at the imperial academy [?] merely magnified ceremonial ornament; holding the classics and debating difficult passages merely drew an admiring throng. Some disputed contentious interpretations of the classics; others laid aside their weapons to expound the canonical arts. Expounding texts in the Lizheng Academy fell shamefully short of true understanding; issuing imperial pronouncements in the Erying Hall brought the shame of having no practical application. It was as though these undertakings awaited their proper moment: the Way does not take effect of itself.
With the advent of our august Ming, these excellent institutions were made manifest. Lecture sessions were inaugurated, and worthy men received in audience by day; the ranks of scholars flourished as in the warmth of spring. Sagely in originating and enlightened in transmitting, our rulers carried forward the achievements of the Three Kings of remote antiquity. Exalting virtue and broadening their accomplishments, they took as their sole model the plans of the Two Emperors. If we enumerate all that has been recorded of earlier times, none ultimately surpasses…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
今日恭惟
皇帝陛下
聰明天縱
仁孝性成
元良預養於龍潛
大寶嗣承於燕翼
任老成而求賢若渴
開言路而從諫如流費罷不經慰愬海內徯蘇
之望稅蠲有等答天下仰德之心謂經史
備載夫古今而帝王恒資於講習謙讓未
===
遑他務遵行首及
經筵
丹幄初開
翠華至止士集章縫之盛彙進儒紳函抽匱
室之藏庋分典籍挈其綱領皆精神心術
之微鑒彼勸懲悉治忽興衰之故屢進貫
生之席肆聞箕子之疇
聖學造端
punctuated: 今日。恭惟皇帝陛下，聰明天縱，仁孝性成。元良預養於龍潛，大寶嗣承於燕翼。任老成而求賢若渴，開言路而從諫如流。費罷不經，慰愬海內徯蘇之望；稅蠲有等，答天下仰德之心。謂經史備載夫古今，而帝王恒資於講習，謙讓未遑他務，遵行首及經筵。丹幄初開，翠華至止。士集章縫之盛，彙進儒紳；函抽匱室之藏，庋分典籍。挈其綱領，皆精神心術之微；鑒彼勸懲，悉治忽興衰之故。屢進貫生之席，肆聞箕子之疇。聖學造端
translation_en:
…today. We respectfully consider that Your Majesty the Emperor possesses Heaven-given intelligence and is humane and filial by nature. Your virtues as heir apparent were nurtured beforehand while the dragon remained hidden; you succeeded to the imperial throne through the provision made for posterity. You employ mature and experienced men and thirst for worthy talent; you open the channels of expression and accept remonstrance as readily as water flows. You abolish irregular expenditures, comforting those who voice grievances [?] and fulfilling the hopes of all within the seas who await relief; you remit taxes in graded measure, answering the hearts of all under Heaven who look up to your virtue.

You hold that the classics and histories fully record past and present, and that emperors and kings constantly draw upon their exposition and study. In your modest deference, you have had no leisure for other affairs: foremost among the practices you observed were the Classics Colloquia. The vermilion curtains had scarcely opened when your kingfisher-feather standard arrived. Scholars gathered in a splendid assembly of Confucian caps, and the ranks of learned gentlemen advanced together. Cases were drawn from the repositories, and the canonical books were arranged on their shelves. In grasping their guiding principles, you explore the subtleties of the spirit and the workings of the mind; in examining their encouragements and admonitions, you discern the causes of order and disorder, rise and decline. Repeatedly you draw nearer the mat of Scholar Guan [?], and thus hear the exposition of Jizi’s categories. Your sagely learning takes its beginning…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
帝心有冀匡非泥章句之陳迹寔有契精一之
眞傳者也〔臣〕等位忝臣鄰職司獻納仰
木天而致慶望學海以颺言徒懷野人曝背
之忱殊乏大臣格心之術伏願
乾行不息
咸受有終窒欲防微均宮中府中之體詔𢧐
諫懸重師氏保氏之官
至德妙於篤恭神道設教
大化成於丕顯以經法天
===
君道與師道而並隆文運偕
國運而共泰〔臣〕等無任瞻
天仰
聖欣躍屛營之至謹奉
表稱
賀以
聞
第叁塲
策五道
punctuated:
帝心有冀匡，非泥章句之陳迹，寔有契精一之眞傳者也。〔臣〕等位忝臣鄰，職司獻納，仰木天而致慶，望學海以颺言。徒懷野人曝背之忱，殊乏大臣格心之術。伏願乾行不息，咸受有終；窒欲防微，均宮中府中之體；詔𢧐諫，懸重師氏保氏之官。至德妙於篤恭，神道設教；大化成於丕顯，以經法天。君道與師道而並隆，文運偕國運而共泰。〔臣〕等無任瞻天仰聖、欣躍屛營之至，謹奉表稱賀以聞。

第叁塲
策五道
translation_en:
…the imperial heart hopes for corrective guidance [?]; this is no mere attachment to the stale traces of textual explication, but a true accord with the authentic transmission of refinement and single-mindedness. We, your servants, unworthily occupy positions close to the throne and are charged with presenting counsel. Gazing up toward the lofty palace of learning, we offer congratulations; looking toward the ocean of learning, we raise our voices. We possess only the sincerity of the rustic who wished to offer his sovereign the warmth of the sun upon his back, and utterly lack the great minister’s art of rectifying his ruler’s heart.

We humbly wish that Your Majesty may move ceaselessly, as Heaven does, and bring all to a successful conclusion; restrain desires and guard against the slightest beginnings of error, applying the same principles within the palace and in the government offices; command remonstrance [?], and accord high importance to the offices of Preceptor and Guardian. May supreme virtue attain its subtle perfection through earnest reverence, establishing instruction through the numinous Way; may great transforming influence achieve glorious manifestation, taking Heaven as its model through the Classics. May the Way of the ruler and the Way of the teacher flourish together, and may the fortunes of letters prosper alongside those of the state. We, your servants, look up to Heaven and revere Your Sagely Majesty with boundless joy and trembling awe. We respectfully present this memorial of congratulations for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
第一問
張四端
同考試官教授徐　批〔此策義明詞雅篇終推廣〕
聖學之要精切詳盡必其素蓄忠愛之誠者敬服敬服
考試官教諭王　批〔立意醇正條答詳明〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔靖獻之忠見諸詞表佳士也〕
帝王之學其有本乎正其心而已矣正心
之功其有要乎主於敬而已矣蓋敬者德
之聚聖學之所以成始而成終者也心者
===
身之主萬化之所從以出者也求之至近
而有以御乎遠操之至約而有以該乎博
故主敬以正心正心以爲學此圖萬世道
學之源帝王致治之本也粤稽諸古堯舜
之執中文武之建極而聖學傳心之要肇
於此矣故語四聖之心者曰兢兢業業曰
敬止敬勝何莫非一敬之流通也語四聖
之治者曰時雍風動曰咸和永清何莫非
一心之默運也降及後世帝王之學不講
punctuated:
第一問
張四端
同考試官教授徐，批〔此策義明詞雅，篇終推廣〕聖學之要，精切詳盡，必其素蓄忠愛之誠者。敬服，敬服！
考試官教諭王，批〔立意醇正，條答詳明〕
考試官教諭劉，批〔靖獻之忠，見諸詞表，佳士也〕
帝王之學，其有本乎？正其心而已矣。正心之功，其有要乎？主於敬而已矣。蓋敬者，德之聚，聖學之所以成始而成終者也。心者，身之主，萬化之所從以出者也。求之至近，而有以御乎遠；操之至約，而有以該乎博。故主敬以正心，正心以爲學，此圖萬世道學之源、帝王致治之本也。粤稽諸古，堯舜之執中，文武之建極，而聖學傳心之要肇於此矣。故語四聖之心者，曰兢兢業業，曰敬止敬勝，何莫非一敬之流通也？語四聖之治者，曰時雍風動，曰咸和永清，何莫非一心之默運也？降及後世，帝王之學不講
translation_en:
First Policy Question
Zhang Siduan
Associate Examiner Xu, Prefectural School Professor, comments: 〔“This policy essay is clear in meaning and elegant in expression. At its close, it develops more fully〕 the essentials of the learning of the sages, with precision, pertinence, detail, and thoroughness. Its author must long have nurtured sincere loyalty and devotion. I admire him, I admire him!”
Examiner Wang, County School Instructor, comments: 〔“Its underlying conception is sound and orthodox; its responses to the individual points are detailed and clear.”〕
Examiner Liu, County School Instructor, comments: 〔“The loyalty with which he devotes himself to service is manifest in his words. He is an excellent scholar.”〕
Does the learning of emperors and kings have a foundation? It consists simply in rectifying the mind. Does the work of rectifying the mind have an essential principle? It consists simply in making reverence its guiding principle. Reverence is where virtues converge; through it, the learning of the sages achieves both its beginning and its completion. The mind is the ruler of the person and the source from which all transformations issue. Seek it in what is nearest, and one has the means to govern what is distant; grasp it in what is most concise, and one has the means to encompass what is vast. Thus one makes reverence the guiding principle in order to rectify the mind, and rectifies the mind in order to pursue learning. This is [?] the source of the learning of the Way for all ages and the foundation upon which emperors and kings bring about good government.
Examining antiquity, we find Yao and Shun holding fast to the Mean, and Kings Wen and Wu establishing the supreme standard: here originated the essential principle of the transmission of the mind in the learning of the sages. Thus, when speaking of the minds of these four sages, the texts say “ever cautious and vigilant,” and “abiding in reverence” and “reverence overcoming [negligence].” How could any of these be other than the pervading operation of reverence alone? When speaking of the government of these four sages, the texts say “then there was harmony” and “[the people were] moved as by the wind,” and “all were in concord” and “lasting tranquillity.” How could any of these be other than the silent working of the one mind? Coming down to later ages, the learning of emperors and kings was no longer cultivated…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
心法之要靡傳若石渠之校閱經史虎觀
之講論異同其博覈非不精也集賢館之
招延崇正院之講說其立志非不勤也然
而身心罔益聖學奚裨此漢唐宋之治所
以不古若者有由然矣洪惟我
太祖高皇帝肇造區夏日親儒臣與朱善
講家人而闡誠實威嚴之道與許存仁
講洪範而知天人感應之理與王禕
講大學而著德厚人懷之義於論語則取節
===
用愛人之言爲治國之良規於孟子則言
仁義之道爲時君所當用眞有以妙契千
古聖人之藴矣然豈無所本乎蓋其
觀心有亭言此心之虛靈乘氣機以出入而
嘆操存之難
存心有録舉災祥之譴告爲天心之仁愛而
思致感消復之道載觀
聖政記首篇諭輔臣之言
曰心爲一身主帥常自點檢防閑此身使不
punctuated:
心法之要靡傳。若石渠之校閱經史、虎觀之講論異同，其博覈非不精也；集賢館之招延、崇正院之講說，其立志非不勤也。然而身心罔益，聖學奚裨？此漢唐宋之治所以不古若者，有由然矣。
洪惟我太祖高皇帝肇造區夏，日親儒臣，與朱善講家人而闡誠實威嚴之道，與許存仁講洪範而知天人感應之理，與王禕講大學而著德厚人懷之義。於論語則取節用愛人之言，爲治國之良規；於孟子則言仁義之道，爲時君所當用。眞有以妙契千古聖人之藴矣！然豈無所本乎？蓋其觀心有亭，言此心之虛靈，乘氣機以出入，而嘆操存之難；存心有録，舉災祥之譴告爲天心之仁愛，而思致感消復之道。載觀聖政記首篇諭輔臣之言，曰：「心爲一身主帥，常自點檢，防閑此身，使不
translation_en:
…the essentials of the method of cultivating the mind were no longer transmitted. The collation and study of the classics and histories at the Shiqu Pavilion, and the discussion of differing interpretations at the White Tiger Hall, were certainly meticulous in their extensive investigations. The recruitment of scholars at the Jixian Academy and the lectures at the Chongzheng Institute [?] certainly showed diligence of purpose. Yet they brought no benefit to personal conduct or the mind: how did they advance the learning of the sages? There was thus a reason why the governance of the Han, Tang, and Song did not equal that of antiquity.
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao, when he founded his rule over the Chinese realm, associated daily with Confucian officials. In discussing the Family hexagram with Zhu Shan, he elucidated the way of sincerity and dignified authority. In discussing the Great Plan with Xu Cunren, he understood the principles of mutual response between Heaven and humanity. In discussing the Great Learning with Wang Yi, he made clear the meaning of winning people's allegiance through abundant virtue. From the Analects he took the injunction to be sparing in expenditure and to cherish the people as an excellent rule for governing the state. Of the Mencius, he said that its way of benevolence and righteousness ought to be employed by the rulers of his time. He truly achieved a profound accord with the deepest teachings of the sages throughout the ages! Yet could this have been without a foundation? For contemplating the mind, he had a pavilion: he spoke of the mind's empty, numinous awareness, moving outward and inward with the workings of vital energy, and lamented the difficulty of holding fast to and preserving it. For preserving the mind, he had a written record: he treated the admonitions conveyed by calamities and auspicious signs as expressions of the benevolent care of Heaven's mind, and pondered how to evoke a response, dispel calamity, and restore good order [?]. Further, in the opening section of the Record of Sagely Governance, we read his words of instruction to his assisting ministers: “The mind is the commander of the whole person. I constantly examine myself and keep this body under restraint, so that it does not …

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
妄動自信巳能若防閑此心使不妄動尚
難能也以是爲學非即古帝王正心之學
乎曁我
皇考世宗肅皇帝丕承
鴻業詢謀輔臣齋以
九五名而獨秉夫剛健中正之德室以
恭默名而有取於惟玄惟默之義以
豳風名亭重稼穡之艱難也以
無逸名殿戒豫樂之縱恣也眞有以銳意千
===
古聖人之訓矣求其所本則以
敬一有箴欲弗參以二三之私
心箴有註欲不移以聲色之累及伏讀
經書備覽之詩有曰乃作金丹蔔分置諸宮
牆庶使隨所讀養吾靈臺光則宴安之地
皆懋學之功游息之天皆養心之助矣以
是爲學非即我
太祖正心之學乎
聖祖
punctuated: 妄動，自信巳能；若防閑此心，使不妄動，尚難能也。」以是爲學，非即古帝王正心之學乎？曁我皇考世宗肅皇帝，丕承鴻業，詢謀輔臣，齋以九五名，而獨秉夫剛健中正之德；室以恭默名，而有取於惟玄惟默之義；以豳風名亭，重稼穡之艱難也；以無逸名殿，戒豫樂之縱恣也。眞有以銳意千古聖人之訓矣！求其所本，則以敬一有箴，欲弗參以二三之私；心箴有註，欲不移以聲色之累。及伏讀經書備覽之詩，有曰：「乃作金丹蔔，分置諸宮牆。庶使隨所讀，養吾靈臺光。」則宴安之地，皆懋學之功；游息之天，皆養心之助矣。以是爲學，非即我太祖正心之學乎？聖祖
translation_en:
…act recklessly, I am confident I can already do this; but to guard and restrain this mind so that it does not act recklessly is still difficult.” To pursue learning in this way—is this not precisely the learning through which the ancient emperors and kings rectified their minds?

Then our imperial deceased father, Emperor Shizong, posthumously honored as Su, grandly inherited the great imperial enterprise and consulted his assisting ministers. He named his study Jiuwu, “Nine in the Fifth Place,” and personally upheld the virtues of strength, vigor, centrality, and correctness. He named his chamber Gongmo, “Reverent Silence,” drawing upon the meaning of profundity and silence. He named a pavilion Binfeng, “Airs of Bin,” to emphasize the hardships of sowing and reaping. He named a hall Wuyi, “Against Idleness,” to warn against unrestrained indulgence in ease and pleasure. Truly, he applied himself resolutely to the teachings of the sages throughout the ages!

If we seek the foundation of this, he composed an Admonition on Reverence for the One, wishing not to adulterate it with divided private interests; he supplied a commentary on the Admonition on the Mind, wishing not to be diverted by the encumbrances of sensual pleasures. Moreover, reverently reading his poem on the Comprehensive Survey of the Classics, we find these words: “Then I made jindanbo [?], distributing them along the walls of the various palaces, hoping that, wherever I read, I might nourish the radiance of my mind.” Thus, places of tranquil repose all served his diligent learning, and times of recreation and rest all aided the cultivation of his mind. To pursue learning in this way—is this not precisely our Taizu’s learning of rectifying the mind?

The sage ancestor…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
神孫授受一道是以致治之隆直有以媲古帝
王而陋漢唐宋於不足言矣恭惟我
皇上嗣承大統即位之初慎選儒臣
開經筵以進講勸學興禮
幸胄監以崇儒其所以緝熙
聖學者蓋誠近紹
祖考之弘烈而遠追帝王之道統者矣執事猶
以靖獻之忠望於諸生者忠臣愛君無已
之盛心也然愚以爲
===
經筵雖設而儒臣之進講者或憚於威嚴而
不足以盡其啓沃之忠講劘雖勤而
聖心之開納者或蔽以己私而不足以弘其虛
受之度必也
和顏色以接引之
開誠心以嘉納之究極乎聖賢道德性命之
微反復乎古今治亂興衰之故如堯之衢
室之問舜之總章之訪武王之受丹書於
太公訪洪範於箕子可也猶未也
punctuated: 神孫授受一道，是以致治之隆，直有以媲古帝王，而陋漢唐宋於不足言矣。恭惟我皇上嗣承大統，即位之初，慎選儒臣，開經筵以進講，勸學興禮，幸胄監以崇儒。其所以緝熙聖學者，蓋誠近紹祖考之弘烈，而遠追帝王之道統者矣。執事猶以靖獻之忠望於諸生者，忠臣愛君無已之盛心也。然愚以爲，經筵雖設，而儒臣之進講者或憚於威嚴，而不足以盡其啓沃之忠；講劘雖勤，而聖心之開納者或蔽以己私，而不足以弘其虛受之度。必也和顏色以接引之，開誠心以嘉納之，究極乎聖賢道德性命之微，反復乎古今治亂興衰之故，如堯之衢室之問、舜之總章之訪、武王之受丹書於太公、訪洪範於箕子，可也。猶未也。
translation_en:
…and his divine descendants transmitted and received a single Way. Thus the excellence of their government could indeed rival that of the emperors and kings of antiquity, relegating the Han, Tang, and Song to an inferiority scarcely worth discussing. We reverently consider how Our Emperor succeeded to the imperial line and, at the outset of his reign, carefully selected Confucian officials and inaugurated the Classics Colloquium for the delivery of lectures. He encouraged learning, promoted ritual, and visited the Imperial University to honor Confucian scholarship. His means of bringing ever greater brilliance to his sagely learning truly carry forward, in the nearer past, the great achievements of his imperial forebears and reach back, in the distant past, to pursue the transmission of the Way of the ancient emperors and kings. That you, honored examiners, nevertheless expect us students to offer loyal and considered service reflects the abundant devotion of loyal ministers whose love for their ruler knows no end.

Yet in my humble view, although the Classics Colloquium has been established, the Confucian officials who lecture there may be intimidated by imperial majesty and thus unable fully to discharge their loyal duty to enlighten and nourish the imperial mind. Although lectures and scholarly discussions are diligently pursued, the sagely mind’s receptiveness may be obscured by private preoccupations, preventing the full exercise of its capacity to receive counsel with an open mind. His Majesty must therefore welcome and encourage them with a kindly countenance, and open his sincere heart to receive their counsel graciously. He should investigate to the utmost the subtle teachings of the sages and worthies concerning the Way, virtue, human nature, and Heaven’s mandate, and repeatedly examine the causes of order and disorder, rise and decline, past and present. It would be fitting to emulate Yao’s inquiries in the Hall at the Crossroads, Shun’s consultations in the Hall of General Assembly, and King Wu’s receiving the Cinnabar Writing from Taigong and consulting Jizi about the Great Plan. Yet even this is not enough.

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
深宮邃閫之中無異於
清廟明堂之上
燕閒宥密之地不殊於
視朝臨御之時而又左右前後罔非吉士侍
御僕從無非正人如古之所謂暬御之箴
朦瞍之誦盤盂之銘几杖之戒無不備具
可也然猶未也儉夫壬人懼其有以惑吾
心也馳騁遊畋懼其有以蕩吾心也土木
聲色貨利懼其有以荒吾心也則絶之惟
===
恐其不遠遠之惟恐其不速而又日
親大臣以咨決政務日
覽章奏以習練
朝綱則無一念而非敬無一事而非學庶可
以涵養
聖心薰陶德性
聖敬日躋而
聖治益隆矣若徒循經筵之故事朝而講夕而
退聲色遊逸之欲紛於外而理欲邪正之
punctuated: 深宮邃閫之中，無異於清廟明堂之上；燕閒宥密之地，不殊於視朝臨御之時。而又左右前後罔非吉士，侍御僕從無非正人，如古之所謂暬御之箴、朦瞍之誦、盤盂之銘、几杖之戒，無不備具，可也。然猶未也。儉夫壬人，懼其有以惑吾心也；馳騁遊畋，懼其有以蕩吾心也；土木聲色貨利，懼其有以荒吾心也。則絶之惟恐其不遠，遠之惟恐其不速。而又日親大臣，以咨決政務；日覽章奏，以習練朝綱。則無一念而非敬，無一事而非學，庶可以涵養聖心，薰陶德性，聖敬日躋，而聖治益隆矣。若徒循經筵之故事，朝而講，夕而退，聲色遊逸之欲紛於外，而理欲邪正之
translation_en: …Within the deep palace and its secluded inner chambers, conduct should be no different from that in the pure ancestral temple or the Hall of Light; in places of private repose, it should be no different from that when presiding over court audiences. Moreover, those to the left and right, before and behind, should all be worthy men, and attendants and servants should all be upright. Everything spoken of in antiquity—the admonitions of intimate attendants, the recitations of blind musicians, the inscriptions on basins and bowls, and the warnings on armrests and staffs—should be fully provided. This would be fitting, yet even this is not enough. As for petty men [?] and flatterers, fear that they may delude your mind; as for riding and hunting, fear that they may unsettle your mind; as for building projects, music and sensual pleasures, wealth and profit, fear that they may lead your mind astray. Thus, cut them off, fearing only that they are not far enough removed; distance yourself from them, fearing only that you do not do so swiftly enough. Furthermore, draw close to the great ministers daily to consult on and decide affairs of government, and read memorials daily to become thoroughly versed in the guiding principles of court government. Then no thought will lack reverence, and no undertaking will be other than learning. In this way, you may nurture your sagely mind and cultivate your moral nature, so that your sagely reverence rises daily and your sagely governance flourishes ever more. If, however, you merely follow the established routines of the Classics Colloquium, with lectures in the morning and withdrawal in the evening, while desires for music, sensual pleasures, excursions, and ease crowd in from without, and principle and desire, perversity and rectitude…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
幾淆於中則雖有忠誠如程頤直諒如蘇
軾婉切如范祖禹者亦何補哉芹曝之見
如斯請以是爲
聖天子典學之助
第二問
梁　喬
同考試官教授程　批〔剖析前聞卓有定見且文氣蒼〕
古非摭拾浮詞者比也取之
考試官教諭王　批〔理明而詞雅〕
===
考試官教諭劉　批〔精確不浮足占所養〕
帝王之治天下有道焉率之以忠孝以端
建極之本迪之以謨訓以弘錫類之仁何
也忠孝者竭臣子之分也而萬世之綱常
繫焉不建其極則無以端本而正其趨謨
訓者明忠孝之理也而一代之典章昭焉
不錫其類則無以弘仁而達其化故惇典
明倫建極於上也有君父之道焉彰軌貞
教錫類於下也有臣民之訓焉所謂帝王
punctuated:
幾淆於中，則雖有忠誠如程頤、直諒如蘇軾、婉切如范祖禹者，亦何補哉？芹曝之見如斯，請以是爲聖天子典學之助。

第二問

梁　喬

同考試官教授程　批〔剖析前聞，卓有定見，且文氣蒼〕古，非摭拾浮詞者比也，取之。

考試官教諭王　批〔理明而詞雅〕

考試官教諭劉　批〔精確不浮，足占所養〕

帝王之治天下有道焉：率之以忠孝，以端建極之本；迪之以謨訓，以弘錫類之仁。何也？忠孝者，竭臣子之分也，而萬世之綱常繫焉；不建其極，則無以端本而正其趨。謨訓者，明忠孝之理也，而一代之典章昭焉；不錫其類，則無以弘仁而達其化。故惇典明倫，建極於上也，有君父之道焉；彰軌貞教，錫類於下也，有臣民之訓焉。所謂帝王
translation_en:
…the incipient stirrings become confused within, then even men as loyal and sincere as Cheng Yi, as upright and trustworthy as Su Shi, or as tactful yet earnest as Fan Zuyu could be of what help? Such are my humble views, offered like celery or the warmth of the sun. I ask that they serve as an aid to the sagely Son of Heaven’s constant pursuit of learning.

Second Question

Liang Qiao

Comment by Associate Examiner Cheng, Professor: “His analysis of earlier learning displays decidedly firm judgment, and his prose has an antique vigor. He is beyond comparison with those who merely gather empty phrases. Accept him.”

Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: “His reasoning is clear and his language elegant.”

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “Precise and sound, without superficiality: this amply reveals his cultivation.”

There is a Way by which emperors and kings govern the realm: they lead it through loyalty and filial piety, thereby setting right the foundation for establishing the supreme standard; they guide it through counsels and instructions, thereby extending the benevolence that spreads goodness to others. Why is this? Loyalty and filial piety mean fulfilling to the utmost one’s duties as a subject and a son; upon them depend the cardinal bonds and constant norms of all ages. Unless the supreme standard is established, there is no means of setting the foundation right and directing people’s course aright. Counsels and instructions clarify the principles of loyalty and filial piety; through them the institutions and regulations of a dynasty are made manifest. Unless goodness is extended to others, there is no means of broadening benevolence and spreading its transforming influence. Thus, giving full weight to the enduring norms and clarifying human relationships establishes the supreme standard above: herein lies the Way of rulers and fathers. Making proper models manifest and rendering instruction upright extends goodness below: herein lies instruction for subjects and common people. What is meant by emperors and kings…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
以忠孝治天下也不在此與覩此則我
文皇帝孝順事實之纂
章皇帝歷代臣鑒之錄其有得於建極錫類之
義而爲萬古不刊之鉅典矣請詳之甞聞
君父之尊猶天然人臣以天道事君者謂
之忠人子以天道事親者謂之孝是忠孝
之義也然曷以徵哉吾徵於所處矣處常
易處變難處易則事隱處難則名高大舜
聖人也而父瞽瞍周公聖人也而君成王
===
二者皆難之也二聖人者無常無變處之
一也故夔夔之誠化瞽瞍爲聖父几几之
度致成王爲賢君而忠孝稱大矣自舜周
之名高而臣子盡職愈難自臣子之職難
而忠孝立論愈著考諸論記有分忠孝爲
二者自分之殊者言之也如子夏竭力致
身之類是已非裂道也有合忠孝爲一者
自理之一者言之也如曾子孝者所以事
君之類是已非綴語也載稽孝經一書立
punctuated:
以忠孝治天下也，不在此與？覩此，則我文皇帝《孝順事實》之纂、章皇帝《歷代臣鑒》之錄，其有得於建極錫類之義，而爲萬古不刊之鉅典矣。請詳之。
甞聞君父之尊猶天，然人臣以天道事君者謂之忠，人子以天道事親者謂之孝，是忠孝之義也。然曷以徵哉？吾徵於所處矣。處常易，處變難；處易則事隱，處難則名高。大舜，聖人也，而父瞽瞍；周公，聖人也，而君成王。二者皆難之也。二聖人者，無常無變，處之一也。故夔夔之誠化瞽瞍爲聖父，几几之度致成王爲賢君，而忠孝稱大矣。自舜周之名高，而臣子盡職愈難；自臣子之職難，而忠孝立論愈著。考諸《論》《記》，有分忠孝爲二者，自分之殊者言之也，如子夏竭力致身之類是已，非裂道也；有合忠孝爲一者，自理之一者言之也，如曾子孝者所以事君之類是已，非綴語也。載稽《孝經》一書，立
translation_en:
…Is this not where the meaning of governing the realm through loyalty and filial piety lies? Viewed in this light, our Emperor Wen’s compilation of Accounts of Filial Obedience and Emperor Zhang’s recording of the Mirror for Ministers of Successive Dynasties grasp the meaning of establishing the highest standard and extending its blessings to others. They are thus great canonical works that shall remain unaltered for all ages. Allow me to explain in detail.
I have heard that the exalted position of ruler and father is like that of Heaven. For a minister to serve his ruler according to the Way of Heaven is called loyalty; for a son to serve his parents according to the Way of Heaven is called filial piety. Such is the meaning of loyalty and filial piety. But how can this be substantiated? I substantiate it by examining the circumstances people faced. It is easy to deal with ordinary circumstances, but difficult to deal with extraordinary ones. When circumstances are easy, one’s deeds remain obscure; when they are difficult, one’s reputation rises high. The great Shun was a sage, yet his father was Gusou; the Duke of Zhou was a sage, yet his ruler was King Cheng. Both relationships presented difficulties. These two sages responded in the same way, whether circumstances were ordinary or extraordinary. Thus Shun’s reverent sincerity transformed Gusou into a sage father, and the Duke of Zhou’s dignified bearing brought King Cheng to become a worthy ruler. Their loyalty and filial piety were therefore acclaimed as great.
Once the reputations of Shun and the Duke of Zhou had risen so high, fulfilling the duties of minister and son became still more difficult. As those duties became more demanding, explanations of loyalty and filial piety became ever more explicit. Examining the Analects and the Book of Rites, we find passages that distinguish loyalty and filial piety as two things: these speak from the standpoint of the difference between one’s respective duties. Zixia’s words about exerting all one’s strength in serving one’s parents and devoting one’s person to serving one’s ruler are an example. They do not split the Way apart. Other passages unite loyalty and filial piety as one: these speak from the standpoint of the unity of their underlying principle. Master Zeng’s words that filial piety is the means by which one serves one’s ruler are an example. They are not merely words strung together. Further examining the Classic of Filial Piety, its establishment of…

title: 隆慶元年山西鄉試錄
text:
敎尤切其書云何自天子諸侯卿大夫士
庶人各因嚴敎敬因親敎愛而孝道之論
備矣迨及漢世忠經作焉作忠經者馬融
倣孝經之意也經爲十八章列聖君冢官
百工守宰及兆人等事雖其中援引敷析
不能盡當而論忠及孝理亦悉矣亦未可
少之也二經具存各有攸指雖稱垂範立
敎之言罔裨率善勵行之典迨我
聖祖開基敷德闡敎
===
諭官之詞明孝之章所以上承天道下示民
極者至惓切也
成祖文皇帝體天經地義之懿敦萬善百行之
本爰採諸書
作爲孝順事實自漢文以上帝王之孝得四
人焉狄仁傑以下公卿士庶之孝得二百
三人焉析之事類系之詩章其義精矣
成祖序其謂大足以動天地感鬼神微足以化
强暴格鳥獸孚草木是誠達天人之微通
punctuated:
敎尤切。其書云何？自天子、諸侯、卿大夫、士、庶人，各因嚴敎敬，因親敎愛，而孝道之論備矣。迨及漢世，《忠經》作焉。作《忠經》者，馬融倣《孝經》之意也。經爲十八章，列聖君、冢官、百工、守宰及兆人等事。雖其中援引敷析不能盡當，而論忠及孝，理亦悉矣，亦未可少之也。二經具存，各有攸指，雖稱垂範立敎之言，罔裨率善勵行之典。迨我聖祖開基，敷德闡敎，諭官之詞、明孝之章，所以上承天道、下示民極者，至惓切也。
成祖文皇帝體天經地義之懿，敦萬善百行之本，爰採諸書，作爲《孝順事實》。自漢文以上，帝王之孝得四人焉；狄仁傑以下，公卿士庶之孝得二百三人焉。析之事類，系之詩章，其義精矣。成祖序，其謂大足以動天地、感鬼神，微足以化强暴、格鳥獸、孚草木，是誠達天人之微、通
translation_en:
…its teaching is especially earnest. What does this book say?
